Ant Vespera.ant: Respóndens autem Petrus, * dixit ad Jesum: Dómine, bonum est nos hic esse.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Then answered Peter, * and said unto Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here.

Ant Vespera.ant: Adhuc eo loquénte, * ecce nubes lúcida obumbrávit eos.
Ant Vespera.antEng: While he yet spake, * behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lauréntius * ingréssus est Martyr, et conféssus est nomen Dómini Jesu Christi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lawrence * went in to be a martyr, and acknowledged the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lauréntius * bonum opus operátus est, qui per signum crucis cæcos illuminávit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lawrence wrought a good work, * in that with the sign of the Cross he gave sight to the blind.

Ant Laudes.ant: Adhǽsit * ánima mea post te, quia caro mea igne cremáta est pro te, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O my God, my soul cleaveth * fast after thee, for my flesh hath been burnt with fire for thy sake.

Ant Laudes.ant: Misit Dóminus * Angelum suum, et liberávit me de médio ignis, et non sum æstuátus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord hath sent His Angel, * and hath delivered me out of the midst of the fire, so that I am not scorched.

Ant Laudes.ant: Beátus Lauréntius * orábat, dicens: Grátias tibi ago, Dómine, quia jánuas tuas íngredi mérui.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The blessed Lawrence prayed * and said: I give thee thanks, O Lord, that Thou hast made me worthy to enter within thy gates.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Quo progréderis * sine fílio, pater? quo, sacérdos sancte, sine minístro próperas?
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Father, whither goest thou * without thy son? Holy Priest, dost thou fare hence without a Deacon?

Ant Matutinum.ant: Noli me derelínquere, * pater sancte, quia thesáuros tuos jam expéndi, quos tradidísti mihi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Leave me not, holy father, * for I have spent already thy treasures, which thou gavest unto me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Non ego te désero, * fili, neque derelínquo; sed majóra tibi debéntur pro Christi fide certámina.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I leave thee not, my son, neither forsake thee; * there awaiteth thee for Christ's truth a sterner wrestling than mine.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus Lauréntius * orábat, dicens: Dómine Jesu Christe, Deus de Deo, miserére mihi servo tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The blessed Lawrence prayed * and said: O Lord Jesus Christ, God of God, take pity upon me thy servant.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dixit Románus * ad beátum Lauréntium: Vídeo ante te júvenem pulchérrimum, festína me baptizáre.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Romanus said * to Blessed Lawrence: I see in front of thee a very well-favoured young man; make haste to baptize me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus Lauréntius * dixit: Mea nox obscúrum non habet, sed ómnia in luce claréscunt.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The blessed Lawrence said: The darkness is no darkness to me, * but the night is all as clear as morning, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Strinxérunt * córporis membra pósita super cratículam: subiciéntibus prunas insúltat Levíta Christi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They laid him upon the grating, and stretched out his limbs; * Christ's Levite held in derision them that brought the live coals.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Igne me examinásti, * et non est invénta in me iníquitas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou hast tried me with fire, * and found no wickedness in me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Interrogátus * te Dóminum conféssus sum, assátus grátias ago.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When I was asked, I acknowledged thee to be the Lord; now that I am roasted, I give thee thanks.

Ant Vespera.antEng: Lawrence * went in to be a martyr, and acknowledged the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant Laudes.ant: Assúmpta est María in cælum: * gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Mary hath been taken to heaven; * the Angels rejoice; they praise and bless the Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: María Virgo assúmpta est * ad æthéreum thálamum, in quo Rex regum stelláto sedet sólio.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Virgin Mary hath been taken into the chamber on high, * where the King of kings sitteth on a throne amid the stars.

Ant Laudes.ant: In odórem * unguentórum tuórum cúrrimus: adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te nimis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: We run after thee, on the scent of thy perfumes * the virgins love thee heartily.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedícta * fília tu a Dómino: quia per te fructum vitæ communicávimus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed of the Lord art thou, O daughter, * for by thee we have been given to eat of the fruit (of the tree) of Life.

Ant Laudes.ant: Pulchra es * et decóra, fília Jerúsalem, terríbilis ut castrórum ácies ordináta.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Fair and comely art thou, O daughter of Jerusalem, * terrible as a fenced camp set in battle array.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Exaltáta est * sancta Dei Génetrix super choros Angelórum ad cæléstia regna.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The holy Mother of God is exalted over choirs of Angels * into the heavenly kingdom.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Paradísi portæ * per te nobis apértæ sunt, quæ hódie gloriósa cum Angelis triúmphas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Through thee have the gates of Paradise been thrown open to us, * O thou who this day dost triumph so gloriously among the Angels.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Benedícta tu * in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed art thou among women, * and blessed is the Fruit of thy womb.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sanctificávit * tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Most High * has sanctified His tabernacle.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Gloriósa * prædicántur de te, Virgo María.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Glorious things * are spoken of thee, O Virgin Mary.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Gaude, María Virgo: * cunctas hǽreses sola interemísti in univérso mundo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Rejoice, O Virgin Mary, * thou hast trampled down all the heresies in the whole world.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cæli annúntiant * justítiam ejus, et omnes pópuli vident glóriam ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The heavens shall announce * his justice, and all peoples will see his glory.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cantáte Dómino * cánticum novum: quia mirabília fecit in te, o María.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing to the Lord * a new song, for he hath done marvelous things unto thee, O Mary.

Ant Vespera.ant: Assúmpta est María in cælum: * gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Mary hath been taken to heaven; * the Angels rejoice; they praise and bless the Lord.

Ant Laudes.antEng: The Virgin Mary hath been taken into the chamber on high, * where the King of kings sitteth on a throne amid the stars.

Ant Laudes.ant: In odórem * unguentórum tuórum cúrrimus: adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te nimis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: We run after thee, on the scent of thy perfumes * the virgins love thee heartily.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedícta * fília tu a Dómino: quia per te fructum vitæ communicávimus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed of the Lord art thou, O daughter, * for by thee we have been given to eat of the fruit (of the tree) of Life.

Ant Laudes.ant: Pulchra es * et decóra, fília Jerúsalem, terríbilis ut castrórum ácies ordináta.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Fair and comely art thou, O daughter of Jerusalem, * terrible as a fenced camp set in battle array.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Exaltáta est * sancta Dei Génetrix super choros Angelórum ad cæléstia regna.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The holy Mother of God is exalted over choirs of Angels * into the heavenly kingdom.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Paradísi portæ * per te nobis apértæ sunt, quæ hódie gloriósa cum Angelis triúmphas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Through thee have the gates of Paradise been thrown open to us, * O thou who this day dost triumph so gloriously among the Angels.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Benedícta tu * in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed art thou among women, * and blessed is the Fruit of thy womb.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo: Deus in medio ejus, non commovébitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God shall give her the help of His countenance; * God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sicut lætántium * omnium nostrum habitátio est in te, sancta Dei Genitrix.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Holy Mother of God * all we who dwell in thee are in gladness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Gaude, María Virgo: * cunctas hǽreses sola interemísti in univérso mundo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Rejoice, O Virgin Mary, * thou hast trampled down all the heresies in the whole world.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dignáre me * laudare te, Virgo sacrata: da mihi virtútem contra hostes tuos.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Holy Virgin, my praise by thee accepted be; * give me strength against thine enemies.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Post partum * Virgo invioláta permansisti, Dei Genitrix intercéde pro nobis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: After thy delivery thou still remainest a virgin * undefiled; Mother of God, pray for us.

Ant Vespera.ant: Assúmpta est María in cælum: * gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Mary hath been taken to heaven; * the Angels rejoice; they praise and bless the Lord.

Ant Vespera.ant: María Virgo assúmpta est * ad æthéreum thálamum, in quo Rex regum stelláto sedet sólio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Virgin Mary hath been taken into the chamber on high, * where the King of kings sitteth on a throne amid the stars.

Ant Vespera.ant: In odórem * unguentórum tuórum cúrrimus: adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te nimis.
Ant Vespera.antEng: We run after thee, on the scent of thy perfumes * the virgins love thee heartily.

Ant Vespera.ant: Benedícta * fília tu a Dómino: quia per te fructum vitæ communicávimus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Blessed of the Lord art thou, O daughter, * for by thee we have been given to eat of the fruit (of the tree) of Life.

Ant Vespera.ant: Pulchra es * et decóra, fília Jerúsalem, terríbilis ut castrórum ácies ordináta.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Fair and comely art thou, O daughter of Jerusalem, * terrible as a fenced camp set in battle array.

Ant Laudes.ant: Heródes enim ténuit * et ligávit Joánnem et pósuit in cárcerem propter Herodíadem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: For Herod had laid hold upon John, * and bound him, and put him in prison, for Herodias' sake.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dómine mi rex, * da mihi in disco caput Joánnis Baptístæ.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord my King, * give me in a charger the head of John the Baptist.

Ant Laudes.ant: Puéllæ saltánti * imperávit mater: Nihil áliud petas, nisi caput Joánnis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The damsel danced, * and her mother charged her, saying: See thou ask nothing, but only the head of John.

Ant Laudes.ant: Arguébat * Heródem Joánnes propter Herodíadem, quam túlerat fratri suo Philíppo uxórem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: John had rebuked Herod for Herodias' sake, * his brother Philip's wife, for he had taken her.

Ant Laudes.ant: Da mihi in disco * caput Joánnis Baptístæ. Et contristátus est rex propter jusjurándum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Give me in a charger the head of John the Baptist. * And the King was sorry, for his oath's sake.

Ant Vespera.ant: Heródes enim ténuit * et ligávit Joánnem et pósuit in cárcerem propter Herodíadem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: For Herod had laid hold upon John, * and bound him, and put him in prison, for Herodias' sake.

Ant Vespera.ant: Dómine mi rex, * da mihi in disco caput Joánnis Baptístæ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: O Lord my King, * give me in a charger the head of John the Baptist.

Ant Vespera.ant: Puéllæ saltánti * imperávit mater: Nihil áliud petas, nisi caput Joánnis.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The damsel danced, * and her mother charged her, saying: See thou ask nothing, but only the head of John.

Ant Vespera.ant: Arguébat * Heródem Joánnes propter Herodíadem, quam túlerat fratri suo Philíppo uxórem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: John had rebuked Herod for Herodias' sake, * his brother Philip's wife, for he had taken her.

Ant Vespera.ant: Da mihi in disco * caput Joánnis Baptístæ. Et contristátus est rex propter jusjurándum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Give me in a charger the head of John the Baptist. * And the King was sorry, for his oath's sake.

Ant Laudes.ant: Natívitas gloriósæ * Vírginis Maríæ ex sémine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This day was born the glorious Virgin Mary, * a child of the seed of Abraham, a daughter of the tribe of Judah, a Princess of the lineage of David.

Ant Laudes.ant: Natívitas est hódie * sanctæ Maríæ Vírginis, cujus vita ínclita cunctas illústrat ecclésias.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This day is the Birthday of the holy Virgin Mary, * whose famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.

Ant Laudes.ant: Regáli ex progénie * María exórta refúlget; cujus précibus nos adjuvári, mente et spíritu devotíssime póscimus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Mary was a maiden of illustrious birth, * the daughter of a Kingly race. We earnestly entreat her to help our minds and souls by her prayers.

Ant Laudes.ant: Corde et ánimo * Christo canámus glóriam in hac sacra solemnitáte præcélsæ Genetrícis Dei Maríæ.
Ant Laudes.antEng: With all our heart and with all our soul let us sing praise to Christ * on this the solemn Feast-day of Mary, the mighty Mother of God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cum jucunditáte * Nativitátem beátæ Maríæ celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Jesum Christum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let us keep with rejoicing the Birthday of the Blessed Virgin Mary, * that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant Vespera.ant: Natívitas gloriósæ * Vírginis Maríæ ex sémine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This day was born the glorious Virgin Mary, * a child of the seed of Abraham, a daughter of the tribe of Judah, a Princess of the lineage of David.

Ant Vespera.ant: Corde et ánimo * Christo canámus glóriam in hac sacra solemnitáte præcélsæ Genetrícis Dei Maríæ.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cum jucunditáte * Nativitátem beátæ Maríæ celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Jesum Christum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Let us keep with rejoicing the Birthday of the Blessed Virgin Mary, * that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant Laudes.ant: O magnum pietátis opus: * mors mórtua tunc est, in ligno quando mórtua Vita fuit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O what a work of love was that * when Life and death died together upon the Tree. (Alleluia.)

Ant Laudes.ant: Salva nos, * Christe Salvátor, per virtútem Crucis: qui salvásti Petrum in mari, miserére nobis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Save us, * O Christ the Saviour, save us through the might of thy Cross Thou Who didst save Peter when he was ready to sink in the sea, have mercy upon us. (Alleluia.)

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce Crucem Dómini, * fúgite, partes advérsæ, vicit leo de tribu Juda, radix David, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, the Cross of the Lord! * fly, ye ranks of the adversary! The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, hath prevailed. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Nos autem gloriári * opórtet in Cruce Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: But us it behoveth to glory * in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. (Alleluia.)

Ant Laudes.ant: Per signum Crucis * de inimícis nostris líbera nos, Deus noster.
Ant Laudes.antEng: By thy Cross' holy sign, * Jesus, guard this soul of mine from my ghostly enemy. (Alleluia.)

Ant Matutinum.ant: Nóbile lignum * exaltátur, Christi fides rútilat, dum Crux ab ómnibus venerátur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the noble tree's uplifting, * and the nations bending low, see a proof that Christ hath triumphed o'er the legions of the foe.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sancta Crux * extóllitur a cunctis régibus, virga régia erígitur, in qua Salvátor triumphávit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the Holy Cross * uplifted, see the rod of power exalted, wherewithal King Jesus triumphed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: O Crux venerábilis, * quæ salútem attulísti míseris, quibus te éfferam præcóniis, quóniam vitam nobis cǽlitem præparásti.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Cross most gracious, * from whose aspect health to sickly souls is given, with what praises shall I praise thee, who hast brought us life from heaven?

Ant Matutinum.ant: O Crucis victória * et admirábile signum, in cælésti cúria fac nos captáre triúmphum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: For all that feel sin's fiery wound ensign of health the Saviour see! * May we as conquerors be found through Him Who triumphed on the tree.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Funéstæ mortis * damnátur supplícium, dum Christus, in Cruce, nostra destrúxit víncula críminum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When by the Saviour on the Cross * the bonds of sin were riven, we by His chastisement were healed, and death to death was given.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Rex exaltátur * in ǽthera, cum nóbile trophǽum Crucis ab univérsis christícolis adorátur per sǽcula.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Before the saving Cross of Christ * all Christians bend in prayer, and glory is ascribed to Him who dreadly triumphed there.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adorámus te, Christe, * et benedícimus tibi, quia per Crucem tuam redemísti mundum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: We adore thee, O Christ, * and we bless thee, because through thy Cross Thou hast redeemed the world.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Per lignum * servi facti sumus, et per sanctam Crucem liberáti sumus: fructus árboris sedúxit nos, Fílius Dei redémit nos, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: By a tree * were we brought into bondage, and by the Holy Cross are we set free. The fruit of a tree beguiled us; the Son of God hath brought us back. Alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Salvátor mundi, * salva nos: qui per Crucem et sánguinem tuum redemísti nos, auxiliáre nobis, te deprecámur, Deus noster.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Save us, O Saviour of the world, * Who hast redeemed us by thy Cross and Blood; help us, we beseech thee, O our God!

Ant Laudes.ant: Quo ábiit * diléctus tuus, o pulchérrima mulíerum? quo declinávit diléctus tuus, et quærémus eum tecum?
Ant Laudes.antEng: Whither is thy beloved gone, * O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Recédite a me, * amáre flebo, nolíte incúmbere, ut consolémini me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Look away from me. * I will weep bitterly. Labour not to comfort me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Non est ei * spécies neque decor, et vídimus eum, et non erat aspéctus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: He hath no form nor comeliness, * and when we shall see him there is no beauty that we should desire him.

Ant Laudes.ant: A planta pedis * usque ad vérticem cápitis non est in eo sánitas.
Ant Laudes.antEng: From the sole of the foot * even unto the head, there is no soundness in it.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fulcíte me flóribus, * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples for I am swooning with love.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Multiplicáti sunt * qui tríbulant me, multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They are increased that trouble me; * many are they that rise up against me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Paravérunt sagíttas suas * in pháretra, ut sagíttent in obscúro rectos corde.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They make ready their arrows in the quiver, * that they may privily shoot at the upright in heart.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Defécit in dolóre * vita mea, et anni mei in gemítibus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My life is spent with grief, * and my years with sighing.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factum est cor meum * tamquam cera liquéscens in médio ventris mei.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My heart is like * melting wax in the midst of my bowels.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus, vitam meam * annuntiávi tibi: posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O God, I have declared my life * unto thee: Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Fuérunt mihi * lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My tears have been * my meat day and night.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Intendérunt arcum * rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They bend their bow, * even bitter words, that they may shoot in secret at the perfect.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ánima mea * turbáta est valde: sed tu, Dómine, úsquequo?
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My soul * is sore vexed, but Thou, O Lord, how long.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus adjútor * in tribulatiónibus quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God is our help * in trouble, which is come upon us exceedingly.

Ant Vespera.antEng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples for I am swooning with love.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Concússum est mare, * et contrémuit terra, ubi Archángelus Míchaël descendébat de cælo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The sea was moved * and the earth quaked, when the Archangel Michael descended from heaven.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Laudémus Dóminum, * quem laudant Ángeli, quem Chérubim et Séraphim, Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus proclámant.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let us praise the Lord, * Whom the Angels do praise, unto Whom Cherubim and Seraphim do cry, Holy, Holy, Holy.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ascéndit * fumus arómatum in conspéctu Dómini de manu Ángeli.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The smoke of the incense ascended up * before the Lord, out of the Angel's hand.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Míchaël Archángele, * veni in adjutórium pópulo Dei.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Archangel Michael, * come to help God's people.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Míchaël * præpósitus paradísi, quem honoríficant Angelórum cives.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Archangel Michael * is the Vice-Roy of Paradise, and the Angels that are the dwellers therein do hold him in worship.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Gloriósus * apparuísti in conspéctu Dómini: proptérea decórem índuit te Dóminus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou wast manifested in thy glory * in the Presence of the Lord. Therefore the Lord hath clothed thee with majesty.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ángelus Archángelus Míchaël, * Dei núntius pro animábus justis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Angel Michael the Archangel, * he is the messenger whom God sendeth to all the souls of the righteous. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Data sunt ei * incénsa multa, ut adoléret ea ante altáre áureum, quod est ante óculos Dómini.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: There was given unto him * much incense, that he should offer it upon the golden altar which is before the eyes of the Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Multa magnália * de Michaéle Archángelo, qui, fortis in prǽlio, fecit victóriam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Great things are spoken * of Michael the Archangel, who waxed valiant in fight, and won the victory.

Ant Vespera.antEng: This day is the Birthday of the holy Virgin Mary, * whose famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.

Ant Vespera.antEng: Mary was a maiden of illustrious birth, * the daughter of a Kingly race. We earnestly entreat her to help our minds and souls by her prayers.

Ant Vespera.ant: Corde et ánimo * Christo canámus glóriam in hac sacra solemnitáte præcélsæ Genetrícis Dei Maríæ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With all our heart and with all our soul let us sing praise to Christ * on this the solemn Feast-day of Mary, the mighty Mother of God.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cum jucunditáte * Nativitátem beátæ Maríæ celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Jesum Christum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Let us keep with rejoicing the Birthday of the Blessed Virgin Mary, * that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant Laudes.ant: Angelis suis * Deus mandávit de te, ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: God hath given His Angels charge over thee, * to keep thee in all thy ways.

Ant Laudes.ant: Laudémus Dóminum, * quem laudant Angeli, quem Chérubim et Séraphim, sanctus, sanctus, sanctus proclámant.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let us praise the Lord, * Whom the Angels do praise, unto Whom Cherubim and Seraphim do cry, Holy, Holy, Holy.

Ant Laudes.ant: Angeli eórum * semper vident fáciem Patris mei, qui est in cælis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In heaven their Angels do always behold the face of My Father, * Which is in heaven.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíctus Deus, * qui misit Angelum suum, et éruit servos suos qui credidérunt in eum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed be God, * Who sent His Angel, and delivered His servants that trusted in Him.

Ant Laudes.ant: Laudáte Deum, * omnes Angeli ejus: laudáte eum, omnes Virtútes ejus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise ye God, * all His Angels Praise ye Him, all His hosts.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus, Deus * cæli et terræ, ipse mittet Angelum suum coram te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord God of heaven and earth shall send His Angel before thee.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus meus * misit Angelum suum et conclúsit ora leónum, et non nocuérunt mihi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My God hath sent His Angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Bene ambulétis, * et Dóminus sit in itínere vestro, et Angelus ejus comitétur vobíscum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Go prosperously, and the Lord be with you in your journey, and His Angel keep you company.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum essem vobíscum, * per voluntátem Dei eram: ipsum benedícite et cantáte ei.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When I came unto you, by the will of God I came; bless Him, and give Him thanks.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tollens se Angelus Dómini, * qui præcedébat castra Israël, ábiit post eos.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Angel of the Lord, which went before the camp of Israel, removed, and went behind them.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Immíttet Angelus Dómini * in circúitu timéntium eum, et erípiet eos.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear Him, and delivereth them.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Misit Dóminus * Angelum suum, qui percússit omnem virum robústum et bellatórem, et príncipem exércitus regis Assyriórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord sent His Angel, which cut off all the mighty of valour, and the leaders and captains in the camp of the King of Assyria.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adoráte Dóminum * omnes Angeli ejus: audívit, et lætáta est Sion.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Worship the Lord, all ye His Angels! Zion heard, and was glad.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Benedícite Dómino, * omnes Angeli ejus, poténtes virtúte, faciéntes verbum illíus, ad audiéndam vocem sermónum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Bless the Lord, all ye His Angels, that excel in strength, that do His commandments, to hearken unto the voice of His word.

Ant Vespera.ant: Angelis suis * Deus mandávit de te, ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
Ant Vespera.antEng: God hath given His Angels charge over thee, * to keep thee in all thy ways.

Ant Vespera.ant: Laudémus Dóminum, * quem laudant Angeli, quem Chérubim et Séraphim, sanctus, sanctus, sanctus proclámant.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Let us praise the Lord, * Whom the Angels do praise, unto Whom Cherubim and Seraphim do cry, Holy, Holy, Holy.

Ant Vespera.antEng: In heaven their Angels do always behold the face of My Father, * Which is in heaven.

Ant Vespera.antEng: Blessed be God, * Who sent His Angel, and delivered His servants that trusted in Him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Laudáte Deum, * omnes Angeli ejus: laudáte eum, omnes Virtútes ejus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Praise ye God, * all His Angels Praise ye Him, all His hosts.

Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Let us praise the Lord, * Whom the Angels do praise, unto Whom Cherubim and Seraphim do cry, Holy, Holy, Holy.

Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Praise ye God, * all His Angels Praise ye Him, all His hosts.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lætáre, * Virgo Mater; surréxit Christus de sepúlcro.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Rejoice, O Virgin Mother, * Christ is risen from the grave.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ascéndit Deus * in jubilatióne, et Dóminus in voce tubæ.
Ant Laudes.antEng: God is gone up with a shout, * and the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.

Ant Laudes.ant: Spíritus Dómini * replévit orbem terrárum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The spirit of the Lord * hath filled the world.

Ant Laudes.ant: Assúmpta est * María in cælum: gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Mary hath been taken to heaven. * The angels rejoice; they praise and bless the Lord. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Exaltáta est * Virgo María super choros Angelórum, et in cápite ejus coróna stellárum duódecim.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Virgin Mary * hath been exalted over choirs of angels, and upon her head there is a crown of twelve stars.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Angelus Gábriel * nuntiávit Maríæ: et concépit de Spíritu Sancto.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Angel Gabriel * announced unto Mary, and she conceived by the Holy Ghost.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Intrávit María * in domum Zacharíæ, et salutávit Elísabeth.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Mary entered * into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elizabeth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Péperit Fílium suum * primogénitum, et reclinávit eum in præsépio.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: She brought forth her first-born Son, * and laid Him in a manger.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum indúcerent * Jesum paréntes ejus, ut sísterent eum Dómino, Símeon accépit eum in ulnas suas, et benedíxit Deum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When His parents brought in * (the child) Jesus to present Him to the Lord, Simeon took Him up in his arms and blessed God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Requiréntes Jesum * paréntes ejus, invenérunt illum post tríduum in médio doctórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: His parents seeking Jesus * found Him after three days in the midst of the doctors.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cœpit contristári, * et factus est sudor ejus in horto sicut guttæ sánguinis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He began to be very sorrowful, * and in the garden the sweat became as it were drops of blood.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Apprehéndit * Pilátus Jesum, et flagellávit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Pilate took Jesus * and scourged Him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Mílites plecténtes corónam * de spinis, imposuérunt super caput ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The soldiers plaited a crown * of thorns, and put it on His Head.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Crucis impérium * super húmerum ejus: regnávit a ligno Deus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The government was upon His shoulder, * even the cross; from the tree hath God reigned.

Ant Vespera.ant: Quæ est ista, * speciósa sicut colúmba, quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum?
Ant Vespera.antEng: Who is this, * fair as a dove, like a rose-tree planted beside the rivers of waters?

Ant Vespera.ant: Virgo potens, * sicut turris David: mille clípei pendent ex ea, omnis armatúra fórtium.
Ant Vespera.antEng: A virgin most mighty, * like the tower of David, whereon there hung a thousand bucklers, all the shields of valiant men.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ave, María, * grátia plena; Dóminus tecum: benedícta tu in muliéribus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Hail Mary, * full of grace, the Lord is with thee, blessed art thou among women.

Ant Vespera.ant: Benedíxit te Dóminus * in virtúte sua, quia per te ad níhilum redégit inimícos nostros.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord hath blessed thee * by His power, because through thee He hath brought our enemies to nought.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vidérunt eam * fíliæ Sion vernántem in flóribus rosárum, et beatíssimam prædicavérunt.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The daughters of Sion saw her in her spring time, amidst the flowers of the roses, and called her most blessed.

Ant Laudes.ant: Beáta es, * Virgo María, quæ ómnium portásti Creatórem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed art thou, * O Virgin Mary, who didst bear the Creator of all things.

Ant Laudes.ant: Genuísti, * qui te fecit, et in ætérnum pérmanes Virgo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou didst bring him forth * who made thee, and remainest a Virgin for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cum essem párvula, * plácui Altíssimo et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: When I was a little one, * I pleased the Most High, and from my womb I have brought forth God and man.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedícta fília * tu a Dómino, quia per te fructum vitæ communicávimus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Daughter, thou art blessed * of the Lord: for by thee we have partaken of the fruit of life.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vidérunt eam * fíliæ Sion, et beátam dixérunt, et regínæ laudavérunt eam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The daughters of Sion, * saw her, and called her blessed; and the queens praised her.

Ant Vespera.ant: Beáta es, * Virgo María, quæ ómnium portásti Creatórem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Blessed art thou, * O Virgin Mary, who didst bear the Creator of all things.

Ant Vespera.ant: Genuísti, * qui te fecit, et in ætérnum pérmanes Virgo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thou didst bring him forth * who made thee, and remainest a Virgin for ever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cum essem párvula, * plácui Altíssimo et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: When I was a little one, * I pleased the Most High, and from my womb I have brought forth God and man.

Ant Vespera.ant: Benedícta fília * tu a Dómino, quia per te fructum vitæ communicávimus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Daughter, thou art blessed * of the Lord: for by thee we have partaken of the fruit of life.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vidérunt eam * fíliæ Sion, et beátam dixérunt, et regínæ laudavérunt eam.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The daughters of Sion, * saw her, and called her blessed; and the queens praised her.

Ant Laudes.ant: Missus est * Angelus Ráphaël ad Tobíam et Saram, ut curáret eos.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Angel Raphael was sent * unto Tobias and Sara to heal them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ingréssus Angelus * ad Tobíam, salutávit eum, et dixit: Gáudium sit tibi semper.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Angel went in * unto Tobias, and said: Joy be ever with thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Forti ánimo * esto, Tobía: in próximo enim est ut a Deo curéris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Be of good courage, Tobias, * for it is nigh at hand that God shall heal thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedícite Deum cæli, * et coram ómnibus vivéntibus confitémini illi, quia fecit vobíscum misericórdiam suam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Bless ye the God of Heaven, * and confess Him before all living, for He hath had mercy upon you.

Ant Laudes.ant: Pax vobis, * nolíte timére: Deum benedícite, et cantáte illi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Peace be unto you, * fear not, bless ye God, and give praise to Him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Egréssus Tobías * invénit júvenem præcínctum, et quasi parátum ad ambulándum, et, ignórans quod Angelus esset, salutávit eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When Tobias went in, * he found a young man with his loins girded, and as it were ready to set forth, and knowing not that it was an Angel, he saluted him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Angelus Ráphaël * seípsum occúltans, ait: Ego sum Azarías, magni Ananíæ fílius.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Angel Raphael * hid himself, and said: I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the Great.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sanum ducam * fílium tuum in regiónem Medórum, et sanum tibi redúcam, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I will bring thy son safely * into the land of the Medes, and bring him back safely unto thee again, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dixit autem Angelus: * Apprehénde bránchiam piscis, et trahe eum extra aquas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And the Angel said: * Take the fish by the gill, and draw him out of the water.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Obsecro te, * Azaría frater, ut dicas mihi, quod remédium habébunt ista, quæ de pisce serváre jussísti.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Tell me, I pray thee, * brother Azarias, to what use is that which thou hast bidden me keep of the fish.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Lúmina fel sanat, * sed virtus cordis et jécoris diáboli expéllit potestátem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The gall is a healing to the eyes, * but the virtue of the heart and the liver putteth the power of the devil to flight.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Est hic Sara * Raguélis fília; quæ tibi conjúgio dábitur, et omnis substántia ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Here is Sara * the daughter of Raguel, who shall be given unto thee to wife, and all her substance with her.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Septem viros hábuit, * quos dæmónium oppréssit; tímeo ne mihi símile contíngat.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: She hath had seven husbands, * who were all strangled by an evil spirit; I am afraid lest the like should befall me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Per tres dies * oratióni cum uxóre tua vacábis, ut in sémine Abrahæ benedictiónem in fíliis consequáris.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Spend three days * in prayer with thy wife, that thou mayest obtain the blessing of sons, in the seed of Abraham.

Ant Vespera.ant: Missus est * Angelus Ráphaël ad Tobíam et Saram, ut curáret eos.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Angel Raphael was sent * unto Tobias and Sara to heal them.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: Pilate took Jesus * and scourged Him.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: The soldiers plaited a crown * of thorns, and put it on His Head.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: The government was upon His shoulder, * even the cross; from the tree hath God reigned.

Ant Vespera.ant: Quæ est ista, * speciósa sicut colúmba, quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum?
Ant Vespera.antEng: Who is this, * fair as a dove, like a rose-tree planted beside the rivers of waters?

Ant Vespera.ant: Virgo potens, * sicut turris David: mille clípei pendent ex ea, omnis armatúra fórtium.
Ant Vespera.antEng: A virgin most mighty, * like the tower of David, whereon there hung a thousand bucklers, all the shields of valiant men.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ave, María, * grátia plena; Dóminus tecum: benedícta tu in muliéribus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Hail Mary, * full of grace, the Lord is with thee, blessed art thou among women.

Ant Vespera.ant: Benedíxit te Dóminus * in virtúte sua, quia per te ad níhilum redégit inimícos nostros.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord hath blessed thee * by His power, because through thee He hath brought our enemies to nought.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vidérunt eam * fíliæ Sion vernántem in flóribus rosárum, et beatíssimam prædicavérunt.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The daughters of Sion saw her in her spring time, amidst the flowers of the roses, and called her most blessed.

Ant Laudes.ant: Suscitábit * Deus cæli regnum quod commínuet et consúmet univérsa regna, et ipsum stabit in ætérnum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The God of heaven * will set up a kingdom that shall break in pieces and shall consume all these kingdoms, and itself shall stand for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dedit ei Dóminus * potestátem et honórem et regnum; et omnes pópuli, tribus et linguæ ipsi sérvient.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord gave him * power and glory, and a kingdom; and all peoples, tribes and tongues shall serve him.

Ant Laudes.ant: Exíbunt aquæ vivæ * de Jerúsalem; et erit Dóminus Rex super omnem terram.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Living waters shall go out * from Jerusalem; and the Lord shall be king over all the earth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Magnificábitur * usque ad términos terræ, et erit iste pax.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Now shall he be magnified * even to the ends of the earth, and this man shall be our peace.

Ant Laudes.ant: Gens et regnum * quod non servíerit tibi, períbit: et gentes solitúdine vastabúntur.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The nation and the kingdom * that will not serve thee, shall perish: and the Gentiles shall be wasted with desolation.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego autem * constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, prǽdicans præcéptum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I have been set up * as King by Him on Sion, His holy mountain, proclaiming His decree.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Glória * et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine: ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honor, O Lord, putting all things under His feet.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Reach up * you ancient portals, that the King of glory may come in.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sedébit * Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord is enthroned * as King forever; may the Lord bless his people with peace.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Virga directiónis, * virga regni tui: proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: A tempered rod * is thy royal scepter; therefore shall nations praise thee forever and ever.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Psállite * Regi nostro, psállite: quóniam Rex magnus super omnem terram.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing praise to our King * sing praise; for he is the great King over all earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Benedicéntur in ipso * omnes tribus terræ; omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In Him * shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed; all the nations shall proclaim His greatness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Et ego primogénitum * ponam illum: excélsum præ régibus terræ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And I will make Him * the firstborn, highest of the kings of the earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Thronus ejus * sicut sol in conspéctu meo: et sicut luna perfécta in ætérnum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: His throne * shall be like the sun before Me; like the moon, which remains forever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Pacíficus * vocábitur, et thronus ejus erit firmíssimus in perpétuum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: He shall be called * Peaceable, and his throne shall be most firm for ever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Regnum ejus * regnum sempitérnum est, et omnes reges sérvient ei et obédient.
Ant Vespera.antEng: His kingdom * is an everlasting kingdom, and all kings shall serve him, and shall obey him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce Vir Oriens * nomen ejus: sedébit et dominábitur, et loquétur pacem géntibus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold a man, the Orient * is his name: he shall sit and rule, and shall speak peace to the Gentiles.

Ant Vespera.ant: Dóminus * judex noster, Dóminus légifer noster: Dóminus Rex noster, ipse salvábit nos.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord * is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver: the Lord is our king, he will save us.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce dedi te * in lucem géntium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extrémum terræ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold, I have given thee * to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Suscitábit * Deus cæli regnum quod commínuet et consúmet univérsa regna, et ipsum stabit in ætérnum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The God of heaven * will set up a kingdom that shall break in pieces and shall consume all these kingdoms, and itself shall stand for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dedit ei Dóminus * potestátem et honórem et regnum; et omnes pópuli, tribus et linguæ ipsi sérvient.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord gave him * power and glory, and a kingdom; and all peoples, tribes and tongues shall serve him.

Ant Laudes.ant: Exíbunt aquæ vivæ * de Jerúsalem; et erit Dóminus Rex super omnem terram.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Living waters shall go out * from Jerusalem; and the Lord shall be king over all the earth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Magnificábitur * usque ad términos terræ, et erit iste pax.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Now shall he be magnified * even to the ends of the earth, and this man shall be our peace.

Ant Laudes.ant: Gens et regnum * quod non servíerit tibi, períbit: et gentes solitúdine vastabúntur.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The nation and the kingdom * that will not serve thee, shall perish: and the Gentiles shall be wasted with desolation.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego autem * constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, prǽdicans præcéptum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I have been set up * as King by Him on Sion, His holy mountain, proclaiming His decree.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Glória * et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine: ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honor, O Lord, putting all things under His feet.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Reach up * you ancient portals, that the King of glory may come in.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sedébit * Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
Virga directiónis, * virga regni tui: proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: R. In heaven and on earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Psállite * Regi nostro, psállite: quóniam Rex magnus super omnem terram.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord is enthroned * as King forever; may the Lord bless his people with peace.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Benedicéntur in ipso * omnes tribus terræ; omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: A tempered rod * is thy royal scepter; therefore shall nations praise thee forever and ever.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Et ego primogénitum * ponam illum: excélsum præ régibus terræ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing praise to our King * sing praise; for he is the great King over all earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Thronus ejus * sicut sol in conspéctu meo: et sicut luna perfécta in ætérnum.

Ant Vespera.ant: Pacíficus * vocábitur, et thronus ejus erit firmíssimus in perpétuum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: He shall be called * Peaceable, and his throne shall be most firm for ever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Regnum ejus * regnum sempitérnum est, et omnes reges sérvient ei et obédient.
Ant Vespera.antEng: His kingdom * is an everlasting kingdom, and all kings shall serve him, and shall obey him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce Vir Oriens * nomen ejus: sedébit et dominábitur, et loquétur pacem géntibus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold a man, the Orient * is his name: he shall sit and rule, and shall speak peace to the Gentiles.

Ant Vespera.ant: Dóminus * judex noster, Dóminus légifer noster: Dóminus Rex noster, ipse salvábit nos.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord * is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver: the Lord is our king, he will save us.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce dedi te * in lucem géntium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extrémum terræ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold, I have given thee * to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vidi turbam magnam, * quam dinumeráre nemo póterat, ex ómnibus géntibus, stantes ante thronum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I beheld, and, lo, great multitude, which no man could number, * of all nations, (and kindreds, and people, and tongues,) stood before the throne.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et omnes Ángeli * stabant in circúitu throni, et cecidérunt in conspéctu throni in fácies suas, et adoravérunt Deum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And all the Angels stood round about the throne, * (and about the Elders, and the four living creatures,) and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Redemísti nos, * Dómine Deus, in sánguine tuo ex omni tribu, et lingua, et pópulo, et natióne, et fecísti nos Deo nostro regnum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou, O Lord God, hast redeemed us by thy Blood, * out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation, and hast made us a kingdom unto our God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedícite Dóminum * omnes elécti ejus: ágite dies lætítiæ, et confitémini illi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Bless the Lord, all ye His chosen, * keep holiday, and extol Him.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hymnus * ómnibus Sanctis ejus: fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi: glória hæc est ómnibus sanctis ejus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The praise of all His Saints, * even of the children of Israel, a people near unto Him; this honour have all His Saints.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Novit Dóminus * viam justórum, qui in lege ejus meditántur die ac nocte.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord knoweth the way of the righteous, * who in His Law do meditate day and night.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Mirificávit * Dóminus Sanctos suos, et exaudívit eos clamántes ad se.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath set apart for Himself them that are holy, * and when they called, He hath heard them.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Admirábile est * nomen tuum, Dómine: quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctos tuos, et constituísti eos super ópera mánuum tuárum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: How excellent is thy Name, O Lord, Who hast crowned thy Saints with glory and honour, * and madest them to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, * qui operáti sunt justítiam, habitábunt in tabernáculo tuo, et requiéscent in monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They that work righteousness, * O Lord, even they, shall abide in thy tabernacle, and dwell in thy holy Hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Hæc est generátio * quæréntium Dóminum, quæréntium fáciem Dei Jacob.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: This is the generation of them that seek the Lord, * that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Lætámini in Dómino, * et exsultáte justi, et gloriámini omnes recti corde.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye righteous, * and shout for joy, all ye that are upright in heart.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Timéte Dóminum * omnes Sancti ejus, quóniam nihil deest timéntibus eum: ecce óculi Dómini super justos, et aures ejus ad preces eórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O fear the Lord, all ye His Saints, * for there is no want to them that fear Him. Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are open unto their cry.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, spes Sanctórum * et turris fortitúdinis eórum, dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum, et habitábunt in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast been a shelter for thy Saints, * a strong tower from the enemy. Thou hast given the heritage to those that fear thy Name, and they shall abide in thy tabernacle for ever.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Qui dilígitis Dóminum, * lætámini in Dómino, et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Ye that love the Lord, rejoice in the Lord, * and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vidi turbam magnam, * quam dinumeráre nemo póterat, ex ómnibus géntibus, stantes ante thronum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I beheld, and, lo, great multitude, which no man could number, * of all nations, (and kindreds, and people, and tongues,) stood before the throne.

Ant Vespera.ant: Et omnes Ángeli * stabant in circúitu throni, et cecidérunt in conspéctu throni in fácies suas, et adoravérunt Deum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: And all the Angels stood round about the throne, * (and about the Elders, and the four living creatures,) and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God.

Ant Vespera.ant: Redemísti nos, * Dómine Deus, in sánguine tuo ex omni tribu, et lingua, et pópulo, et natióne, et fecísti nos Deo nostro regnum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thou, O Lord God, hast redeemed us by thy Blood, * out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation, and hast made us a kingdom unto our God.

Ant Vespera.ant: Benedícite Dóminum * omnes elécti ejus: ágite dies lætítiæ, et confitémini illi.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Bless the Lord, all ye His chosen, * keep holiday, and extol Him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Hymnus * ómnibus Sanctis ejus: fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi: glória hæc est ómnibus sanctis ejus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The praise of all His Saints, * even of the children of Israel, a people near unto Him; this honour have all His Saints.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dixérunt discípuli * ad beátum Martínum: Cur nos, pater, déseris, aut cui nos desolátos relínquis? Invádent enim gregem tuum lupi rapáces.
Ant Laudes.antEng: His disciples said * unto Blessed Martin: Father, why wilt thou go away from us? or with whom wilt thou leave us orphans? For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dómine, * si adhuc pópulo tuo sum necessárius, non recúso labórem: fiat volúntas tua.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not * to work. thy will be done.

Ant Laudes.ant: O virum ineffábilem, * nec labóre victum, nec morte vincéndum, qui nec mori tímuit, nec vívere recusávit!
Ant Laudes.antEng: Not to be told is this man's glory; * whom work did not and death could not conquer; who neither feared to die, nor refused to live.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oculis ac mánibus * in cælum semper inténtus, invíctum ab oratióne spíritum non relaxábat, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: With eyes and hands lifted up to heaven, * he never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Martínus * Ábrahæ sinu lætus excípitur: Martínus, hic pauper et módicus, cælum dives ingréditur, hymnis cæléstibus honorátur.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Martin is called joyfully into Abraham's bosom. * Martin, who was poor here and of small estimation, entereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Martínus, * adhuc catechúmenus, hac me veste contéxit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: While Martin * is yet a Catechumen, he hath clad Me in this garment.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sanctæ Trinitátis * fidem Martínus conféssus est, et baptísmi grátiam percépit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Martin * confessed the faith of the Holy Trinity, and received the grace of baptism.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego signo crucis, * non clípeo protéctus, aut gálea, hóstium cúneos penetrábo secúrus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Not * in the shelter of a buckler, nor of an helmet, but with the sign of the Cross will I pierce the hosts of the enemy.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Confído in Dómino * quod fília mea, précibus tuis, reddénda sit sanitáti.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I trust * in the Lord that at thy prayers my daughter shall be healed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tetrádius, * cógnita Dei virtúte, ad baptísmi grátiam pervénit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When Tetradius * knew the power of God, he attained unto the grace of baptism.

Ant Matutinum.ant: O ineffábilem virum, * per quem nobis tanta mirácula corúscant!
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Not to be told * is this man's glory, by whom so many wonderful works have been set forth before us!

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus Jesus Christus, * non purpurátum aut diadémate reniténtem, se ventúrum esse prædíxit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord Jesus Christ * said not that He would come clothed in purple or adorned with a crown.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sacérdos Dei, Martíne, * apérti sunt tibi cæli et regnum Patris mei.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Martin, * thou Priest of God, the heavens are open unto thee, yea, and the kingdom of My Father.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sacérdos Dei, Martíne, * pastor egrégie, ora pro nobis Deum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Martin, * thou Priest of God, thou worthy shepherd, pray God on our behalf.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Dixérunt discípuli * ad beátum Martínum: Cur nos, pater, déseris, aut cui nos desolátos relínquis? Invádent enim gregem tuum lupi rapáces.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: His disciples said * unto Blessed Martin: Father, why wilt thou go away from us? or with whom wilt thou leave us orphans? For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: O virum ineffábilem, * nec labóre victum, nec morte vincéndum, qui nec mori tímuit, nec vívere recusávit!
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Not to be told is this man's glory; * whom work did not and death could not conquer; who neither feared to die, nor refused to live.

Ant Vespera 3.antEng: With eyes and hands lifted up to heaven, * he never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Martínus * Ábrahæ sinu lætus excípitur: Martínus, hic pauper et módicus, cælum dives ingréditur, hymnis cæléstibus honorátur.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Martin is called joyfully into Abraham's bosom. * Martin, who was poor here and of small estimation, entereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cantántibus órganis, * Cæcília Dómino decantábat, dicens: Fiat cor meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The musicians played, and Cecilia sang unto the Lord, * saying: Let my heart be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.

Ant Laudes.ant: Valeriánus * in cubículo Cæcíliam cum Angelo orántem invénit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Valerian found Cecilia praying in her chamber, * and with her the Angel.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cæcília * fámula tua, Dómine, quasi apis tibi argumentósa desérvit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Busy like a bee, * O Lord, did thine handmaiden Cecilia serve thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíco te, * Pater Dómini mei Jesu Christi, quia per Fílium tuum ignis exstínctus est a látere meo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I bless thee, O Father of my Lord Jesus Christ, * that through thy Son the fire is gone out round about me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Triduánas * a Dómino popósci indúcias, ut domum meam ecclésiam consecrárem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I have asked the Lord for three days, * that I may consecrate my house as a Church.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cæcília virgo * Almáchium superábat: Tibúrtium et Valeriánum ad corónas vocábat.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Maiden Cecilia * overcame Almachius, and called Tiburtius and Valerian to crowns.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Expánsis mánibus * orábat ad Dóminum, ut eam eríperet de inimícis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: She spread forth her hands * and prayed unto the Lord, that He would deliver her from her enemies.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cilício * Cæcília membra domábat, Deum gemítibus exorábat.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Cecilia subdued her body with haircloth, * and besought God with loud crying.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine Jesu Christe, * seminátor casti consílii, súscipe séminum fructus, quos in Cæcília seminásti.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord Jesus Christ, * Who hast said of abstaining from marriage: He that is able to receive it, let him receive it, accept now the fruits from this seed, which Thou didst sow in the heart of Cecilia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beáta Cæcília * dixit ad Tibúrtium: Hódie te fáteor meum cognátum, quia amor Dei te fecit esse contemptórem idolórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed Cecilia * said unto Tiburtius: Today I call thee my brother, for the love of God hath made thee to cast away idols.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Fiat, Dómine, * cor meum et corpus meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Lord, let my heart * and my body be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Crédimus Christum * Fílium Dei verum Deum esse, qui sibi talem elégit fámulam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Christ, the Son of God, * Who hath chosen unto Himself such an handmaiden, Him we believe to be the true God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Nos sciéntes * sanctum nomen ejus, omníno negáre non póssumus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: We that have known * His Holy Name can by no means deny Him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tunc Valeriánus * perréxit, et signo quod accéperat, invénit sanctum Urbánum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Then Valerian * went his way, and found the holy Urban, by the sign which had been given him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cantántibus órganis, * Cæcília Dómino decantábat, dicens: Fiat cor meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The musicians played, and Cecilia sang unto the Lord, * saying: Let my heart be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.

Ant Vespera.antEng: I have asked the Lord for three days, * that I may consecrate my house as a Church.

Ant Vespera 3.antEng: I have asked the Lord for three days, * that I may consecrate my house as a Church.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oránte * sancto Cleménte, appáruit ei Agnus Dei.
Ant Laudes.antEng: While St. Clement prayed, * there appeared unto him the Lamb of God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Non meis méritis * ad vos me misit Dóminus, vestris corónis partícipem fíeri.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Not for my own merits * hath the Lord sent me unto you, that I may share your crowns.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vidi supra montem * Agnum stantem, de sub cujus pede fons vivus emánat.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I saw on the mountain * the Lamb standing, from beneath whose foot flowed a fountain of living waters.

Ant Laudes.ant: De sub cujus pede * fons vivus emánat: flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei.
Ant Laudes.antEng: From beneath whose foot * a fountain of living waters flowed forth: the stream of the river that maketh glad the city of God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnes gentes * per gyrum credidérunt Christo Dómino.
Ant Laudes.antEng: All the nations * round about believed in Christ the Lord.

Ant Vespera.ant: Oránte * sancto Cleménte, appáruit ei Agnus Dei.
Ant Vespera.antEng: While St. Clement prayed, * there appeared unto him the Lamb of God.

Ant Vespera 3.antEng: All the nations * round about believed in Christ the Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Salve, crux pretiósa, * súscipe discípulum ejus, qui pepéndit in te magíster meus Christus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: God bless thee, precious cross, * be welcome to the follower of Him That hung on thee, even my Master Christ.

Ant Laudes.ant: Beátus Andréas * orábat, dicens: Dómine, Rex ætérnæ glóriæ, súscipe me pendéntem in patíbulo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The blessed Andrew prayed and said: * O Lord, King of everlasting glory, receive me hanging on this gallows.

Ant Laudes.ant: Andréas Christi fámulus, * dignus Dei Apóstolus, germánus Petri, et in passióne sócius.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Andrew was the servant of Christ, * a worthy Apostle of God, the brother of Peter, and likened to Christ and to Peter in his death.

Ant Laudes.ant: Maximílla Christo amábilis * tulit corpus Apóstoli, óptimo loco cum aromátibus sepelívit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Christ's dear handmaid Maximilla took the body * of the Apostle and buried it with spices in an honourable place.

Ant Laudes.ant: Qui persequebántur justum, * demersísti eos, Dómine, in inférno, et in ligno crucis dux justi fuísti.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast caused them that persecuted the just to be swallowed up in hell, * but to the just Thou hast thyself shown the way on the tree of the cross.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vidit Dóminus * Petrum et Andréam, et vocávit eos.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord saw Peter and Andrew, * and He called them.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Veníte post me, * dicit Dóminus, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men, * saith the Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Relíctis rétibus suis, * secúti sunt Dóminum Redemptórem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And they left their nets, * and followed the Lord their Saviour.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dignum sibi Dóminus * computávit Mártyrem, quem vocávit Apóstolum, dum esset in mari, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Whom the Lord called to be His Apostle, * when he was by the sea, him also He counted worthy to be His martyr. Alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Diléxit Andréam * Dóminus in odórem suavitátis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Andrew was to the Lord as a sweet savour, * which He loved exceedingly.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Bíduo vivens * pendébat in cruce beátus Andréas pro Christi nómine, et docébat pópulum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The blessed Andrew hung alive upon the cross for two days * for Christ's Name's sake, and, all the while, he taught the people.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Non me permíttas, Dómine, * fámulum tuum a te separári: tempus est ut commendétur terræ corpus meum, et me ad te veníre jubéas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Suffer not thy servant, O Lord, to be parted from thee * the hour is come to lay my body in the earth, and for thee to bid me come unto thyself.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Andréas vero rogábat pópulum, * ut non impedíret passiónem ipsíus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: But Andrew besought the people * not to hinder his passion.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Accipe me ab homínibus * et redde me magístro meo: ut per te me recípiat, qui per te me redémit, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Welcome me from among men and join me again to my Master; * that, as by thee He redeemed me, so by thee also He may take me unto Himself. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Salve, crux pretiósa, * súscipe discípulum ejus, qui pepéndit in te magíster meus Christus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: God bless thee, precious cross, * be welcome to the follower of Him That hung on thee, even my Master Christ.

Ant Vespera.ant: Beátus Andréas * orábat, dicens: Dómine, Rex ætérnæ glóriæ, súscipe me pendéntem in patíbulo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The blessed Andrew prayed and said: * O Lord, King of everlasting glory, receive me hanging on this gallows.

Ant Vespera.ant: Andréas Christi fámulus, * dignus Dei Apóstolus, germánus Petri, et in passióne sócius.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Andrew was the servant of Christ, * a worthy Apostle of God, the brother of Peter, and likened to Christ and to Peter in his death.

Ant Vespera.ant: Maximílla Christo amábilis * tulit corpus Apóstoli, óptimo loco cum aromátibus sepelívit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Christ's dear handmaid Maximilla took the body * of the Apostle and buried it with spices in an honourable place.

Ant Vespera.ant: Qui persequebántur justum, * demersísti eos, Dómine, in inférno, et in ligno crucis dux justi fuísti.
Ant Vespera.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast caused them that persecuted the just to be swallowed up in hell, * but to the just Thou hast thyself shown the way on the tree of the cross.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tota pulchra * es, María, et mácula originális non est in te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou art all fair, O Mary, * there is no spot of original sin in thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vestiméntum tuum * cándidum quasi nix, et fácies tua sicut sol.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thy raiment * is white as snow, and thy countenance as the sun.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tu glória Jerúsalem, * tu lætítia Israël, tu honorificéntia pópuli nostri.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou art the exaltation of Jerusalem, * thou art the great glory of Israel, thou art the great rejoicing of our nation.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedícta es tu, * Virgo María, a Dómino Deo excélso præ ómnibus muliéribus super terram.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Virgin Mary, * blessed art thou of the Most High God, above all the women upon the earth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Trahe nos, * Virgo immaculáta, post te currémus in odórem unguentórum tuórum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Draw us, * Maiden undefiled, we will run after thee in the odour of thy perfumes.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Admirábile est * nomen tuum, Dómine, in univérsa terra, quia in Vírgine María dignum tibi habitáculum præparásti.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, how excellent is thy Name * in all the earth, Who hast made thee a worthy tabernacle in the Virgin Mary.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In sole pósuit * Deus tabernáculum suum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath set * His tabernacle in the sun.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In Conceptióne sua * accépit María benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Even in her Conception * did Mary receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of her salvation.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Diffúsa est * grátia in Conceptióne ejus, et speciósa appáruit inter fílias hóminum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Grace is poured into her Conception, * and she is fairer than the daughters of men.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adjúvit eam * Deus mane dilúculo; sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God hath holpen her right early, * the Most High hath hallowed His tabernacle.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Gloriósa * dicta sunt de te, cívitas Dei: fundávit te Dóminus in móntibus sanctis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Glorious things are spoken of thee, O City of God; * the Lord hath laid thy foundation in the holy mountains.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sanctimónia et magnificéntia * in Conceptióne ejus: annuntiáte in ómnibus pópulis glóriam ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Holiness and beauty are in her Conception; * declare her glory among all people.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Lætámini, omnes, * in Dómino: et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Rejoice ye all in the Lord * and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Notum fecit * Dóminus opus suum: in conspéctu géntium revelávit glóriam Genetrícis suæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath made known His salvation; * the glory of His Mother hath He openly showed in the sight of the heathen.

Ant Vespera.antEng: Thou art all fair, O Mary, * there is no spot of original sin in thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vestiméntum tuum * cándidum quasi nix, et fácies tua sicut sol.

Ant Vespera.ant: Tu glória Jerúsalem, * tu lætítia Israël, tu honorificéntia pópuli nostri.

Ant Vespera.ant: Benedícta es tu, * Virgo María, a Dómino Deo excélso præ ómnibus muliéribus super terram.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Virgin Mary, * blessed art thou of the Most High God, above all the women upon the earth.

Ant Vespera.ant: Trahe nos, * Virgo immaculáta, post te currémus in odórem unguentórum tuórum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Draw us, * Maiden undefiled, we will run after thee in the odour of thy perfumes.

Ant Laudes.ant: Conceptio gloriosæ Virginis Mariæ * ex semine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This day was conceived the glorious Virgin Mary, * a child of the seed of Abraham, a daughter of the tribe of Judah, a Princess of the lineage of David.

Ant Laudes.ant: Conceptio est hodie * sanctæ Mariæ Virginis cujus vita inclyta cunctas illustrat ecclesias.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This day is the Conception of the holy Virgin Mary, * whose famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.

Ant Laudes.ant: Regali ex progenie * Maria exorta refulget: cujus precibus nos adjuvari mente et spiritu devotissime poscimus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Mary was a maiden of illustrious birth, * the daughter of a Kingly race. We earnestly entreat her to help our minds and souls by her prayers.

Ant Laudes.ant: Corde et animo * Christo canamus gloriam in hac sacra solemnitate præcelsæ Genitricis Dei Mariæ.
Ant Laudes.antEng: With all our heart and with all our soul let us sing praise to Christ * on this the solemn Feast-day of Mary, the mighty Mother of God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cum jucunditate * Conceptionem beatæ Mariæ celebremus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercedat ad Dominum Jesum Christum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let us keep with rejoicing the Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, * that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant Vespera.ant: Conceptio gloriosæ Virginis Mariæ * ex semine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This day was conceived the glorious Virgin Mary, * a child of the seed of Abraham, a daughter of the tribe of Judah, a Princess of the lineage of David.

Ant Vespera.ant: Conceptio est hodie * sanctæ Mariæ Virginis cujus vita inclyta cunctas illustrat ecclesias.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This day is the Conception of the holy Virgin Mary, * whose famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.

Ant Vespera.ant: Regali ex progenie * Maria exorta refulget: cujus precibus nos adjuvari mente et spiritu devotissime poscimus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Mary was a maiden of illustrious birth, * the daughter of a Kingly race. We earnestly entreat her to help our minds and souls by her prayers.

Ant Vespera.ant: Corde et animo * Christo canamus gloriam in hac sacra solemnitate præcelsæ Genitricis Dei Mariæ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With all our heart and with all our soul let us sing praise to Christ * on this the solemn Feast-day of Mary, the mighty Mother of God.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cum jucunditate * Conceptionem beatæ Mariæ celebremus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercedat ad Dominum Jesum Christum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Let us keep with rejoicing the Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, * that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant Laudes.ant: Quæ est ista * quæ procéssit sicut sol, et formósa tamquam Jerúsalem?
Ant Laudes.antEng: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, clear as the sun, fair as the moon, comely as Jerusalem?

Ant Laudes.ant: Vidérunt eam * fíliæ Sion vernántem in flóribus rosárum, et beatíssimam prædicavérunt.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The daughters of Sion * saw her flowering with blossoms of roses, and called her most blessed.

Ant Laudes.ant: Flores apparuérunt * in terra nostra: te laudámus, Sancta Dei Génetrix.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Flowers have appeared * in our land: we praise thee, Holy Mother of God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cantáte ei * cánticum novum: Annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam ejus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Sing ye to him * a new canticle: Declare his glory among the Gentiles.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tu glória * Jerúsalem, tu lætítia Israël, tu honorificéntia pópuli tui.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou art * the glory of Jerusalem, thou art the joy of Israel, thou art the honour of thy people.

Ant Vespera.ant: Quæ est ista * quæ procéssit sicut sol, et formósa tamquam Jerúsalem?
Ant Vespera.antEng: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, clear as the sun, fair as the moon, comely as Jerusalem?

Ant Vespera.antEng: Flowers have appeared * in our land: we praise thee, Holy Mother of God.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cantáte ei * cánticum novum: Annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam ejus.

Ant Vespera.ant: Tu glória * Jerúsalem, tu lætítia Israël, tu honorificéntia pópuli tui.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thou art * the glory of Jerusalem, thou art the joy of Israel, thou art the honour of thy people.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oránte sancta Lúcia, * appáruit ei beáta Agatha, et consolabátur ancíllam Christi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: While St. Lucy was praying, * the blessed Agatha appeared unto her, and consoled the handmaiden of Christ.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lúcia virgo, * quid a me petis quod ipsa póteris præstáre contínuo matri tuæ?
Ant Laudes.antEng: O virgin Lucy, * wherefore askest thou of me what thou canst thyself forthwith obtain for thy mother?

Ant Laudes.ant: Per te, Lúcia virgo, * cívitas Syracusána decorábitur a Dómino Jesu Christo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Through thee, O virgin Lucy, * the city of Syracuse shall be made glorious by the Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíco te, * Pater Dómini mei Jesu Christi, quia per Fílium tuum ignis exstínctus est a látere meo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I bless thee, * O Father of my Lord Jesus Christ, for through thy Son the fire was extinguished round about me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Soror mea, Lúcia, * virgo Deo devóta, quid a me petis, quod ipsa póteris præstáre contínuo matri tuæ?
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lucy, my sister, * thou virgin consecrated to God, wherefore askest thou of me what thou canst thyself forthwith obtain for thy mother?

Ant Laudes.ant: Judǽa et Jerúsalem, * nolíte timére: cras egrediémini, et Dóminus erit vobíscum, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Judah and Jerusalem, * fear not: tomorrow ye shall go out, and the Lord will be with you.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hódie sciétis * quia véniet Dóminus: et mane vidébitis glóriam ejus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This day ye shall know * that the Lord cometh and in the morning, then ye shall see His glory.

Ant Laudes.ant: Crástina die * delébitur iníquitas terræ: et regnábit super nos Salvátor mundi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: On the morrow * the sins of the earth shall be washed away, and the Saviour of the world will be our King.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus véniet, * occúrrite illi, dicéntes: Magnum princípium, et regni ejus non erit finis: Deus, Fortis, Dominátor, Princeps pacis, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord cometh! * Go ye out to meet Him, and say How great is His dominion, and of His kingdom there shall be no end! He is the Mighty God, the Ruler, the Prince of Peace, Alleluia!

Ant Laudes.ant: Crástina erit * vobis salus, dicit Dóminus Deus exercítuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: On the morrow * ye shall be saved, saith the Lord God of hosts.

Ant Laudes.ant: Judǽa et Jerúsalem, * nolíte timére: cras egrediémini, et Dóminus erit vobíscum, allelúja.
