Ant Laudes.antEng: On the morrow * the sins of the earth shall be washed away, and the Saviour of the world will be our King.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus véniet, * occúrrite illi, dicéntes: Magnum princípium, et regni ejus non erit finis: Deus, Fortis, Dominátor, Princeps pacis, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord cometh! * Go ye out to meet Him, and say How great is His dominion, and of His kingdom there shall be no end! He is the Mighty God, the Ruler, the Prince of Peace, Alleluia!

Ant Laudes.ant: Crástina erit * vobis salus, dicit Dóminus Deus exercítuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: On the morrow * ye shall be saved, saith the Lord God of hosts.

Ant Laudes.ant: Judǽa et Jerúsalem, * nolíte timére: cras egrediémini, et Dóminus erit vobíscum, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Judah and Jerusalem, * fear not: tomorrow ye shall go out, and the Lord will be with you.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hódie sciétis * quia véniet Dóminus: et mane vidébitis glóriam ejus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This day ye shall know * that the Lord cometh and in the morning, then ye shall see His glory.

Ant Laudes.ant: Crástina die * delébitur iníquitas terræ: et regnábit super nos Salvátor mundi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: On the morrow * the sins of the earth shall be washed away, and the Saviour of the world will be our King.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus véniet, * occúrrite illi, dicéntes: Magnum princípium, et regni ejus non erit finis: Deus, Fortis, Dominátor, Princeps pacis, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord cometh! * Go ye out to meet Him, and say How great is His dominion, and of His kingdom there shall be no end! He is the Mighty God, the Ruler, the Prince of Peace, Alleluia!

Ant Laudes.ant: Crástina erit * vobis salus, dicit Dóminus Deus exercítuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: On the morrow * ye shall be saved, saith the Lord God of hosts.

Ant Laudes.ant: Quem vidístis, * pastóres? dícite, annuntiáte nobis, in terris quis appáruit? Natum vídimus, et choros Angelórum collaudántes Dóminum, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O ye shepherds, speak, * and tell us what ye have seen; who is appeared in the earth? We saw the newborn Child, and angels singing praise to the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Génuit puérpera * Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Mother brought forth the King, * Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Facta est cum Angelo * multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, * praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus dixit * ad me: Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath said unto Me: * Thou art My Son, this day have I begotten thee.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tamquam sponsus * Dóminus procédens de thálamo suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord is as a bridegroom * coming out of his chamber.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Diffúsa est * grátia in lábiis tuis, proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Grace is poured into thy lips, * therefore God hath blessed thee for ever.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Suscépimus, * Deus, misericórdiam tuam in médio templi tui.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: We have drunk in thy loving-kindness, * O God, in the midst of thy temple.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Oriétur * in diébus Dómini abundántia pacis, et dominábitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the Lord's days * shall abundance of peace arise and flourish.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Véritas de terra * orta est, et justítia de cælo prospéxit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Truth is sprung out of the earth, * and righteousness hath looked down from heaven.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ipse invocábit * me, allelúja: Pater meus es tu, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He shall cry unto Me, alleluia, * Thou art My Father, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Læténtur cæli, * et exsúltet terra ante fáciem Dómini, quóniam venit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let the heavens rejoice, * and let the earth be glad before the Lord, for He cometh.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Notum fecit * Dóminus, allelúja, salutáre suum, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath made known, alleluia, * His salvation, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Rex pacíficus * magnificátus est, cujus vultum desíderat univérsa terra.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The King of Peace * is magnified, whose face the whole earth desireth.

Ant Vespera.ant: Magnificátus est * Rex pacíficus super omnes reges univérsæ terræ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Peaceful King * exceeded all the kings of the whole earth.

Ant Vespera.ant: Compléti sunt * dies Maríæ, ut páreret Fílium suum primogénitum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The days of Mary * were accomplished that she should bring forth her first-born Son.

Ant Vespera.ant: Scitóte * quia prope est regnum Dei: amen dico vobis, quia non tardábit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Know ye that the kingdom * of God is at hand? Amen, I say unto you, it will not tarry.

Ant Vespera.ant: Leváte cápita vestra: * ecce appropínquat redémptio vestra.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Lift up your heads; * behold, your redemption draweth nigh.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lapidavérunt Stéphanum, * et ipse invocábat Dóminum, dicens: Ne státuas illis hoc peccátum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: They stoned Stephen, * calling upon God, and saying: Lay not this sin to their charge.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lápides torréntis * illi dulces fuérunt: ipsum sequúntur omnes ánimæ justæ.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The stones of the brook * were sweet to him; all the souls of the righteous follow him.

Ant Laudes.ant: Adhǽsit ánima mea * post te, quia caro mea lapidáta est pro te, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O my God, my soul followeth hard after thee, * for my flesh hath been stoned for thy sake.

Ant Laudes.ant: Stéphanus vidit * cælos apértos, vidit, et introívit: beátus homo, cui cæli patébant.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Stephen saw the heavens opened; * he saw and entered in; blessed is he unto whom the heavens were opened.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce vídeo * cælos apértos, et Jesum stantem a dextris virtútis Dei.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, I see * the heavens opened, and Jesus standing on the right hand of the power of God.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

Ant Vespera 3.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant Laudes.ant: Valde honorándus est * beátus Joánnes, qui supra pectus Dómini in cena recúbuit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Right worthy of honour * is the blessed Apostle John, who leaned on the Lord's bosom at the Last Supper.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hic est discípulus ille * qui testimónium pérhibet de his: et scimus quia verum est testimónium ejus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This is the disciple * which testifieth of these things, and we know that his testimony is true.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hic est discípulus meus: * sic eum volo manére, donec véniam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This is My disciple * if I will that he tarry till I come?

Ant Laudes.ant: Sunt de hic stántibus, * qui non gustábunt mortem, donec vídeant Fílium hóminis in regno suo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: There be some standing here, * which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man in His kingdom.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce puer meus, * eléctus, quem elégi, pósui super eum Spíritum meum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold My servant, * whom I have chosen, I have put My spirit upon him.

Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant Laudes.ant: Heródes irátus * occídit multos púeros in Béthlehem Judæ civitáte David.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Herod was exceeding wroth, * and slew many children in Bethlehem of Judah, the city of David.

Ant Laudes.ant: A bimátu * et infra occídit multos púeros Heródes propter Dóminum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Herod slew many children * from two years old, and under, for the Lord's sake.

Ant Laudes.ant: Angeli eórum * semper vident fáciem Patris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Their angels * do always behold the face of the Father.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vox in Rama * audíta est, plorátus et ululátus, Rachel plorans fílios suos.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In Rama was there a voice * heard, weeping and mourning, Rachel weeping for her children.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sub throno Dei * omnes Sancti clamant: Víndica sánguinem nostrum, Deus noster.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Under the throne of God * all the saints cry aloud: Avenge our blood, O our God!

Ant Laudes.ant: Vadam ad montem * myrrhæ et ad collem thuris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, * and to the hill of frankincense.

Ant Laudes.ant: Diléctus meus * cándidus et rubicúndus: comæ cápitis ejus sicut púrpura regis vincta canálibus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My beloved * is white and ruddy the hair of his head is like kingly purple, bound in tresses.

Ant Laudes.ant: Quo ábiit * diléctus tuus, o pulchérrima mulíerum? quo diléctus tuus declinávit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Whither is thy beloved gone, * O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside?

Ant Laudes.ant: Fascículus myrrhæ * diléctus meus mihi inter úbera mea commorábitur.
Ant Laudes.antEng: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie betwixt my breasts.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fulcíte me flóribus * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples, for I am swooning with love.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Astitérunt reges terræ, * et príncipes convenérunt in unum advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together against the Lord, and against His Anointed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Voce mea * ad Dóminum clamávi, et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I cried unto the Lord with my voice, and He heard me out of His holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factum est cor meum * tamquam cera liquéscens in médio ventris mei.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My heart is like melting wax in the midst of my bowels.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Inimíci mei * dixérunt mala mihi: Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Mine enemies speak evil of me When shall he die, and his name perish.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus, vitam meam * annuntiávi tibi: posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O God, I have declared my life unto thee, Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Fílii hóminum, * dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: As for the sons of men, their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Intendérunt arcum, * rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They bend their bow, even bitter words, that they may shoot in secret at the perfect.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factus sum * sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am as a man that hath no strength, lying nerveless among the dead.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Replévit me amaritúdine, * inebriávit me absýnthio.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.

Ant Laudes.ant: In illa die * stillábunt montes dulcédinem, et colles fluent lac et mel, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In that day * the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Jucundáre, * fília Sion, et exsúlta satis, fília Jerúsalem, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Sing, O daughter of Zion, * and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce Dóminus véniet, * et omnes Sancti ejus cum eo: et erit in die illa lux magna, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, the Lord shall come, * and all His saints with Him; and it shall come to pass in that day that the light shall be great. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnes sitiéntes, * veníte ad aquas: quǽrite Dóminum, dum inveníri potest, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lo, every one that thirsteth * come ye to the waters: seek ye the Lord while He may be found. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce véniet * Prophéta magnus, et ipse renovábit Jerúsalem, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, a great Prophet * shall arise, and He shall build up a new Jerusalem. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce in núbibus cæli * Dóminus véniet cum potestáte magna, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, the Lord * cometh in the clouds of heaven with great power. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Urbs fortitúdinis * nostræ Sion, Salvátor ponétur in ea murus et antemurále: aperíte portas, quia nobíscum Deus, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Our Zion is a strong city, * the Saviour will God appoint in her for walls and bulwarks; open ye the gates, for God is with us. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce apparébit * Dóminus, et non mentiétur: si moram fécerit, exspécta eum, quia véniet, et non tardábit, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, the Lord * shall appear and not lie though He tarry, wait for Him, because He will come and will not tarry. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Montes et colles * cantábunt coram Deo laudem, et ómnia ligna silvárum plaudent mánibus: quóniam véniet Dominátor Dóminus in regnum ætérnum, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The mountains and the hills * shall break forth before God into singing, and all the trees of the wood shall clap their hands for the Lord the Ruler cometh, and He shall reign for ever and ever. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce Dóminus * noster cum virtúte véniet, et illuminábit óculos servórum suórum, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, our Lord * cometh with power, and He shall lighten the eyes of His servants. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Ecce in núbibus cæli * Dóminus véniet cum potestáte magna, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Behold, the Lord * cometh in the clouds of heaven with great power. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Urbs fortitúdinis * nostræ Sion, Salvátor ponétur in ea murus et antemurále: aperíte portas, quia nobíscum Deus, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Our Zion is a strong city, * the Saviour will God appoint in her for walls and bulwarks; open ye the gates, for God is with us. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Ecce apparébit * Dóminus, et non mentiétur: si moram fécerit, exspécta eum, quia véniet, et non tardábit, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Behold, the Lord * shall appear and not lie though He tarry, wait for Him, because He will come and will not tarry. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Montes et colles * cantábunt coram Deo laudem, et ómnia ligna silvárum plaudent mánibus: quóniam véniet Dominátor Dóminus in regnum ætérnum, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The mountains and the hills * shall break forth before God into singing, and all the trees of the wood shall clap their hands for the Lord the Ruler cometh, and He shall reign for ever and ever. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Ecce Dóminus * noster cum virtúte véniet, et illuminábit óculos servórum suórum, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Behold, our Lord * cometh with power, and He shall lighten the eyes of His servants. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Véniet Dóminus, * et non tardábit, et illuminábit abscóndita tenebrárum, et manifestábit se ad omnes gentes, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord will come, * and will not tarry; He both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make Himself manifest to all people. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Jerúsalem, gaude * gáudio magno, quia véniet tibi Salvátor, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Rejoice greatly, O Jerusalem, * for thy Saviour cometh unto thee. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dabo in Sion * salútem, et in Jerúsalem glóriam meam, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I will place salvation in Zion, * and My glory in Jerusalem. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Montes et omnes colles * humiliabúntur: et erunt prava in dirécta, et áspera in vias planas: veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Every mountain and hill * shall be made low, and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; O Lord, come and make no tarrying. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Juste et pie * vivámus, exspectántes beátam spem, et advéntum Dómini.
Ant Laudes.antEng: We should live * righteously and godly, looking for that blessed hope and the coming of the Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cánite tuba * in Sion, quia prope est dies Dómini: ecce véniet ad salvándum nos, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blow ye the trumpet * in Zion, for the day of the Lord is nigh at hand: behold, He cometh to save us! Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce véniet * desiderátus cunctis géntibus: et replébitur glória domus Dómini, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, the desire * of all nations shall come; and the house of the Lord shall be filled with glory. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Erunt prava * in dirécta, et áspera in vias planas: veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The crooked * shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; O Lord, come, and make no tarrying. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus véniet, * occúrrite illi, dicéntes: Magnum princípium, et regni ejus non erit finis: Deus, Fortis, Dominátor, Princeps pacis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord cometh! * Go ye out to meet Him, and say: How great is His dominion, and of His kingdom there shall be no end! He is the mighty God, the Ruler, the Prince of Peace. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnípotens Sermo tuus, * Dómine, a regálibus sédibus véniet, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thine Almighty Word, * O Lord, shall leap down out of thy royal throne. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Post tríduum * invenérunt Jesum in templo sedéntem in médio doctórum, audiéntem illos, et interrogántem eos.
Ant Laudes.antEng: After three days, * they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them, and asking them questions.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dixit mater Jesu * ad illum: Fili, quid fecísti nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The mother of Jesus said * to him: Son, why hast thou done so to us? Behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.

Ant Laudes.ant: Descéndit Jesus * cum eis, et venit Názareth, et erat súbditus illis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Jesus went down * with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et Jesus proficiébat * sapiéntia, et ætáte, et grátia apud Deum et hómines.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Jesus advanced * in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et dicébant: * Unde huic sapiéntia hæc, et virtútes? Nonne hic est fabri fílius?
Ant Laudes.antEng: And they said: * How came this man by this wisdom and miracles? Is not this the carpenter's son?

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum indúcerent * púerum Jesum paréntes ejus, accépit eum Símeon in ulnas suas, et benedíxit Deum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When his parents * brought the Child Jesus, then Simeon took him up in his arms, and blessed God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ut perfecérunt * ómnia secúndum legem Dómini, revérsi sunt in Galilǽam in civitátem suam Názareth.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When they had performed * all things according to the Law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Puer autem * crescébat, et confortabátur plenus sapiéntia, et grátia Dei erat in illo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And the Child grew, * and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Consúrgens Joseph * accépit púerum et matrem ejus nocte, et secéssit in Ægýptum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When Joseph arose, * he took the young Child and his Mother by night, and departed into Egypt.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph in Ægýpto, dicens: Surge et áccipe púerum et matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And the Angel of the Lord * said in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, Arise, and take the young Child and his Mother, and go into the land of Israel.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Et véniens * habitávit Názareth, ut adimplerétur quod dictum est per Prophétas: Quóniam Nazarǽus vocábitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And he came * and dwelt in a city called Nazareth, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophets: He shall be called a Nazarene.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ibant paréntes Jesu * per omnes annos in Jerúsalem in die solémni Paschæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Now the parents of Jesus * went to Jerusalem every year at the Feast of the Passover.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum redírent, * remánsit puer Jesus in Jerúsalem, et non cognovérunt paréntes ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And when they returned, * the Child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem, and his parents knew not of it.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Non inveniéntes Jesum * regréssi sunt in Jerúsalem, requiréntes eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: But when they found him not, * they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph virum Maríæ; de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: And Jacob * begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

Ant Vespera.ant: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Joseph, fili David, noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The angel of the Lord * appeared to Joseph in his sleep, saying: Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost.

Ant Vespera.ant: Pastóres venérunt * festinántes, et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The shepherds came * with haste; and they found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.

Ant Vespera.ant: Magi, intrántes domum, * invenérunt Púerum cum María, matre ejus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Magi, entering into the house, * found the child with Mary his mother.

Ant Vespera.ant: Erat Pater ejus * et Mater mirántes super his quæ dicebántur de illo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: His father * and mother were wondering at those things which were spoken concerning him.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Post tríduum * invenérunt Jesum in templo sedéntem in médio doctórum, audiéntem illos, et interrogántem eos.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: After three days, * they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them, and asking them questions.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dixit mater Jesu * ad illum: Fili, quid fecísti nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The mother of Jesus said * to him: Son, why hast thou done so to us? Behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.

Ant Laudes.ant: Descéndit Jesus * cum eis, et venit Názareth, et erat súbditus illis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Jesus went down * with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et Jesus proficiébat * sapiéntia, et ætáte, et grátia apud Deum et hómines.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Jesus advanced * in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et dicébant: * Unde huic sapiéntia hæc, et virtútes? Nonne hic est fabri fílius?
Ant Laudes.antEng: And they said: * How came this man by this wisdom and miracles? Is not this the carpenter's son?

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum indúcerent * púerum Jesum paréntes ejus, accépit eum Símeon in ulnas suas, et benedíxit Deum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When his parents * brought the Child Jesus, then Simeon took him up in his arms, and blessed God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ut perfecérunt * ómnia secúndum legem Dómini, revérsi sunt in Galilǽam in civitátem suam Názareth.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When they had performed * all things according to the Law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Puer autem * crescébat, et confortabátur plenus sapiéntia, et grátia Dei erat in illo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And the Child grew, * and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Consúrgens Joseph * accépit púerum et matrem ejus nocte, et secéssit in Ægýptum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When Joseph arose, * he took the young Child and his Mother by night, and departed into Egypt.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph in Ægýpto, dicens: Surge et áccipe púerum et matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And the Angel of the Lord * said in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, Arise, and take the young Child and his Mother, and go into the land of Israel.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Et véniens * habitávit Názareth, ut adimplerétur quod dictum est per Prophétas: Quóniam Nazarǽus vocábitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And he came * and dwelt in a city called Nazareth, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophets: He shall be called a Nazarene.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ibant paréntes Jesu * per omnes annos in Jerúsalem in die solémni Paschæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Now the parents of Jesus * went to Jerusalem every year at the Feast of the Passover.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum redírent, * remánsit puer Jesus in Jerúsalem, et non cognovérunt paréntes ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And when they returned, * the Child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem, and his parents knew not of it.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Non inveniéntes Jesum * regréssi sunt in Jerúsalem, requiréntes eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: But when they found him not, * they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph virum Maríæ; de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: And Jacob * begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

Ant Vespera.ant: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Joseph, fili David, noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The angel of the Lord * appeared to Joseph in his sleep, saying: Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost.

Ant Vespera.ant: Pastóres venérunt * festinántes, et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The shepherds came * with haste; and they found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.

Ant Vespera.ant: Magi, intrántes domum, * invenérunt Púerum cum María, matre ejus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Magi, entering into the house, * found the child with Mary his mother.

Ant Vespera.ant: Erat Pater ejus * et Mater mirántes super his quæ dicebántur de illo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: His father * and mother were wondering at those things which were spoken concerning him.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Magi, intrántes domum, * invenérunt Púerum cum María, matre ejus.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The Magi, entering into the house, * found the child with Mary his mother.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Erat Pater ejus * et Mater mirántes super his quæ dicebántur de illo.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: His father * and mother were wondering at those things which were spoken concerning him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

Ant Vespera.ant: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant Vespera.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oleum effúsum * nomen tuum, ídeo adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thy Name is as oil * poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Scitóte, * quia Dóminus ipse est Deus, cujus nomen in ætérnum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Know ye that the Lord He is God, * and His Name endureth for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sitívit * ánima mea ad nomen sanctum tuum, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My soul thirsteth * for thy Holy Name, O Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíctum * nomen glóriæ tuæ sanctum, et laudábile, et superexaltátum in sǽcula.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed * is the Holy Name of thy glory, and worthy to be praised, and exalted above all for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Júvenes et vírgines, * senes cum junióribus laudáte nomen Dómini, quia exaltátum est nomen ejus solíus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Young men and maidens, * old men and children, praise the Name of the Lord, for His Name alone is exalted.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

Ant Matutinum.ant: In nómine Jesu * omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: At the Name of Jesus, * let every knee bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Confitémini * Dómino, et invocáte nomen ejus: mementóte, quóniam excélsum est nomen ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Praise the Lord, * and call upon His Name; remember that His Name is exalted.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Mémores erunt * nóminis tui, Dómine, in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They shall be mindful * of thy Name, O Lord, unto all generations.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Magnificáte * Dóminum mecum, et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O magnify * the Lord with me, and let us exalt His Name together.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Omnes gentes, * quascúmque fecísti, vénient, et adorábunt coram te, Dómine, et glorificábunt nomen tuum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All nations * whom Thou hast made, shall come and worship before thee, O Lord, and shall glorify thy Name.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cantáte Dómino * et benedícite nómini ejus: annuntiáte de die in diem salutáre ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing unto the Lord, * and bless His Name show forth His salvation from day to day.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Secúndum nomen tuum, * Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: justítia plena est déxtera tua.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: According to thy Name, O God, * so is thy praise unto the ends of the earth; thy right hand is full of righteousness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cantáte Deo, * psalmum dícite nómini ejus: iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum, Dóminus nomen illi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing unto God, * sing praises to His Name; spread a path before Him That rideth upon the heavens the Lord is His Name.

Ant Vespera.ant: Omnis * qui invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Whosoever shall call * on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sanctum et terríbile * nomen ejus, inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Holy and terrible * is His Name; the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ego autem * in Dómino gaudébo, et exsultábo in Deo Jesu meo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Yet will I rejoice * in the Lord I will joy in the God of my salvation.

Ant Vespera.ant: A solis ortu * usque ad occásum laudábile nomen Dómini.
Ant Vespera.antEng: From the rising of the sun * unto the going down of the same the Lord's Name is to be praised.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sacrificábo * hóstiam laudis, et nomen Dómini invocábo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will offer * the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the Name of the Lord.

Ant Vespera.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant Vespera.ant: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

Ant Vespera.ant: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant Laudes.ant: Angelus autem Dómini * descéndit de cælo, et accédens revólvit lápidem, et sedébat super eum, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: For an angel of the Lord * descended from heaven and coming rolled back the stone and sat upon it, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et ecce terræmótus * factus est magnus: Angelus enim Dómini descéndit de cælo, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: There was a great earthquake; * For an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Erat autem * aspéctus ejus sicut fulgur, vestiménta autem ejus sicut nix, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And his countenance * was as lightning and his raiment as snow, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Præ timóre autem ejus * extérriti sunt custódes, et facti sunt velut mórtui, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And for fear of him * the guards were struck with terror and became as dead men, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Respóndens autem Angelus, * dixit muliéribus: Nolíte timére: scio enim quod Jesum quǽritis, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And the angel answering * said to the women: Fear not you: for I know that you seek Jesus, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego sum qui sum, * et consílium meum non est cum ímpiis, sed in lege Dómini volúntas mea est, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am who I am * and my counsel is not with the ungodly, my will is in the law of God, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Postulávi Patrem meum, * allelúja: dedit mihi gentes, allelúja, in hereditátem, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I asked my Father, * alleluia, and he gave me nations, alleluia, as inheritance, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego dormívi, * et somnum cepi: et exsurréxi, quóniam Dóminus suscépit me, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I have slept * and have taken my rest: and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.r: Qui pro nobis pepéndit in ligno, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.vEng: The Lord is risen from the sepulcher, alleluia.
Ant Matutinum.rEng: He, who hangeth on the tree, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.rEng: When they saw the Lord, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph, virum Maríæ, de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Jacob begat Joseph, * the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, Who is called Christ. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Missus est * Ángelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilǽæ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam viro, cui nomen erat Joseph, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Angel Gabriel * was sent from God, unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, to a Virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ascéndit autem * Joseph a Galilǽa de civitáte Názareth in Judǽam, in civitátem David, quæ vocátur Béthlehem, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Joseph also went up * from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, unto Judea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et venérunt festinántes, * et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And they came with haste, * and found Mary and Joseph, and the Babe lying in a manger. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et ipse Jesus * erat incípiens quasi annórum trigínta, ut putabátur, fílius Joseph, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Jesus Himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the Son of Joseph. Alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ángelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et fuge in Ægýptum, et esto ibi usque dum dicam tibi, allelúja
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying Arise, and take the young Child and His Mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word. Alleluia

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ángelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël: defúncti sunt enim qui quærébant ánimam Púeri, allelúja
Ant Matutinum.antEng: An Angel of the Lord appeareth in a dream to Joseph (in Egypt) saying Arise, and take the young Child and His Mother, and go into the land of Israel for they are dead which sought the young Child's life. Alleluia

Ant Matutinum.ant: Consúrgens Joseph, * accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus, et venit in terram Israël: et habitávit in civitáte quæ vocátur Názareth, allelúja
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Joseph arose, and took the young Child and His Mother, and came into the land of Israel, and dwelt in a city called Nazareth. Alleluia

Ant Laudes.ant: Viri Galilǽi, * quid aspícitis in cælum? Hic Jesus qui assúmptus est a vobis in cælum, sic véniet, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Ye men of Galilee, * why stand ye gazing up into heaven? This same Jesus, Which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cumque intueréntur * in cælum eúntem illum, dixérunt, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And while they looked * steadfastly towards heaven, as He went up, they said, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Elevátis mánibus, * benedíxit eis, et ferebátur in cælum, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: He lifted up His Hands, * and blessed them, and was carried up into heaven, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Exaltáte Regem regum, * et hymnum dícite Deo, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Extol the King of kings, * and ascribe praise to God, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vidéntibus illis, * elevátus est, et nubes suscépit eum in cælo, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: While they beheld, * He was taken up, and a cloud received Him in heaven, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Eleváta est * magnificéntia tua super cælos, Deus, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens, O God, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus in templo * sancto suo, Dóminus in cælo, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord is in His holy Temple, * the Lord's throne is in heaven, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: A summo cælo * egréssio ejus, et occúrsus ejus usque ad summum ejus, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: His going out is from the end of heaven, * and his circuit even to the end thereof, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Exaltáre, Dómine, * in virtúte tua: cantábimus et psallémus, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be thou exalted, O Lord, * in thy own strength: we will sing and praise, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Exaltábo te, * Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I will extol thee, * O Lord, for thou hast upheld me, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ascéndit Deus * in jubilatióne, et Dóminus in voce tubæ, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God is ascended * with jubilee, and the Lord with the sound of trumpet, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Nimis exaltátus est, * allelúja: super omnes deos, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He is exalted exceedingly, * alleluia: above all gods, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus in Sion, * allelúja: magnus et excélsus, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord in Sion, * alleluia: is great and high, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus in cælo, * allelúja: parávit sedem suam, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord in heaven, * alleluia: hath prepared his throne, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Exaltáte Regem regum, * et hymnum dícite Deo, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Extol the King of kings, * and ascribe praise to God, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vidéntibus illis, * elevátus est, et nubes suscépit eum in cælo, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: While they beheld, * He was taken up, and a cloud received Him in heaven, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cum compleréntur * dies Pentecóstes, erant omnes páriter in eódem loco, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: When the day of Pentecost was fully come * they were all with one accord in one place, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Spíritus Dómini * replévit orbem terrárum, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Spirit of the Lord * filleth the world, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Repléti sunt omnes * Spíritu Sancto, et cœpérunt loqui, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: They were all filled * with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fontes, et ómnia * quæ movéntur in aquis, hymnum dícite Deo, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: See ye fountains, * and all that move in the waters, ascribe ye praise to God, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Loquebántur * váriis linguis Apóstoli magnália Dei, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Apostles spoke in diverse tongues * the wonderful works of God, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factus est * repénte de cælo sonus adveniéntis spíritus veheméntis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Suddenly there came a sound from heaven * as of a rushing mighty wind, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Confírma hoc, Deus, * quod operátus es in nobis: a templo sancto tuo, quod est in Jerúsalem, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Strengthen, O God, that which Thou hast wrought for us, * because of thy holy Temple at Jerusalem, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Emítte Spíritum tuum, * et creabúntur: et renovábis fáciem terræ, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Send forth thy Spirit, and they shall be created * and Thou shalt renew the face of the earth, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.v: Spíritus Dómini replévit orbem terrárum, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.r: Et hoc quod cóntinet ómnia, sciéntiam habet vocis, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.vEng: The Spirit of the Lord filleth the world, alleluia.
Ant Matutinum.rEng: And That Which containeth all things hath knowledge of the voice, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cum compleréntur * dies Pentecóstes, erant omnes páriter in eódem loco, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: When the day of Pentecost was fully come * they were all with one accord in one place, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Spíritus Dómini * replévit orbem terrárum, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Spirit of the Lord * filleth the world, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Repléti sunt omnes * Spíritu Sancto, et cœpérunt loqui, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: They were all filled * with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Fontes, et ómnia * quæ movéntur in aquis, hymnum dícite Deo, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: See ye fountains, * and all that move in the waters, ascribe ye praise to God, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Loquebántur * váriis linguis Apóstoli magnália Dei, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Apostles spoke in diverse tongues * the wonderful works of God, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Cum compleréntur * dies Pentecóstes, erant omnes páriter in eódem loco, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: When the day of Pentecost was fully come * they were all with one accord in one place, alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Spíritus Dómini * replévit orbem terrárum, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The Spirit of the Lord * filleth the world, alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Repléti sunt omnes * Spíritu Sancto, et cœpérunt loqui, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: They were all filled * with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Fontes, et ómnia * quæ movéntur in aquis, hymnum dícite Deo, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: See ye fountains, * and all that move in the waters, ascribe ye praise to God, alleluia.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Loquebántur * váriis linguis Apóstoli magnália Dei, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The Apostles spoke in diverse tongues * the wonderful works of God, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factus est * repénte de cælo sonus adveniéntis spíritus veheméntis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Suddenly there came a sound from heaven * as of a rushing mighty wind, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Confírma hoc, Deus, * quod operátus es in nobis: a templo sancto tuo, quod est in Jerúsalem, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Strengthen, O God, that which Thou hast wrought for us, * because of thy holy Temple at Jerusalem, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Emítte Spíritum tuum, * et creabúntur: et renovábis fáciem terræ, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Send forth thy Spirit, and they shall be created * and Thou shalt renew the face of the earth, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.vEng: The Comforter, Who is the Holy Ghost. Alleluia.
Ant Matutinum.rEng: He shall teach you all things. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Glória tibi, Trínitas * æquális, una Déitas, et ante ómnia sǽcula, et nunc et in perpétuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Glory be to thee, O equal Trinity * one Deity, from before all ages, so now and for evermore.

Ant Laudes.ant: Laus et perénnis glória * Deo Patri, et Fílio, Sancto simul Paráclito, in sæculórum sǽcula.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise and endless glory be * to God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Paraclete, for ever and ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Glória laudis * résonet in ore ómnium, Patri, genitǽque Proli, Spirítui Sancto páriter resúltet laude perénni.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let the glory of praise * be heard from the mouth of all to the Father, and to the begotten Son; let it equally resound with perpetual praise to the Holy Spirit.

Ant Laudes.ant: Laus Deo Patri, * parilíque Proli, et tibi, Sancte, stúdio perénni, Spíritus, nostro résonet ab ore, omne per ævum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise be to God the Father, * and to his co-equal Son, and to thee, O Holy Ghost: with perpetual delight may it resound from our lips for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ex quo ómnia, * per quem ómnia, in quo ómnia: ipsi glória in sǽcula.
Ant Laudes.antEng: From whom are all things, * through whom are all things, and in whom are all things: to him be glory for evermore.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adésto, unus Deus * omnípotens, Pater, Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be present, O One Almighty God, * Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Te unum * in substántia, Trinitátem in persónis confitémur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: We acknowledge that Thou art One in Being, * and Three in Persons.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Te semper idem * esse, vívere, et intellégere profitémur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: We testify * that thy Being, thy Life, and thine Understanding are One and eternally unchangeable.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Te invocámus, * te laudámus, te adorámus, o beáta Trínitas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Upon thee do we call, * thee do we praise, thee do we worship, O Blessed Trinity.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Spes nostra, * salus nostra, honor noster, o beáta Trínitas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou art our Hope, * Thou art our Salvation, Thou art our glory, O Blessed Trinity.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Líbera nos, * salva nos, vivífica nos, o beáta Trínitas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be Thou our Deliverer, * our Saviour, our Life-giver, O Blessed Trinity.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cáritas * Pater est, grátia Fílius, communicátio Spíritus Sanctus, o beáta Trínitas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Father is Love; * the Son is Grace; the Holy Ghost is Communion. Blessed be the Trinity.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Verax est * Pater, véritas Fílius, véritas Spíritus Sanctus, o beáta Trínitas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Father is Truth; * the Son is Truth; the Holy Ghost is Truth. Blessed be the Trinity.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Pater, * et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus una substántia est, o beáta Trínitas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Being of the Father, * and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, is one. Blessed be the Trinity.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sapiéntia * ædificávit sibi domum, míscuit vinum et pósuit mensam, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Wisdom hath builded her house, * she hath mingled her wine, she hath also furnished her table, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Angelórum esca * nutrivísti pópulum tuum, et panem de cælo præstitísti eis, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou feddest thine Own people * with Angels' food, and didst send them bread from heaven, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Pinguis est panis * Christi, et præbébit delícias régibus, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Out of Christ His bread shall be fat, * and He shall yield royal dainties, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sacerdótes sancti * incénsum et panes ófferunt Deo, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Priests shall be holy; * for the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and the bread of their God, they do offer, [therefore they shall be holy], alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vincénti dabo * manna abscónditum, et nomen novum, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: To him that overcometh will I give of the hidden manna, * and will give him a new name, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Fructum salutíferum * gustándum dedit Dóminus mortis suæ témpore.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord brought forth His fruit in the season of His death, * even that fruit whereof if any man eat, he shall live for ever.

Ant Matutinum.ant: A fructu fruménti * et vini multiplicáti fidéles in pace Christi requiéscunt.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: His faithful ones which are increased by the fruit of His corn and His wine * do lay them down in peace and sleep in Christ.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Communióne cálicis, * quo Deus ipse súmitur, non vitulórum sánguine, congregávit nos Dóminus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Us, being many, hath the Lord made one body, * for we are all partakers of that one cup, which is not the communion of the blood of bulls, but of God Himself.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Memor sit Dóminus * sacrifícii nostri: et holocáustum nostrum pingue fiat.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord remember our offering, * and accept our burnt-sacrifice.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Parátur * nobis mensa Dómini advérsus omnes, qui tríbulant nos.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord prepareth His Table before us * in the presence of our enemies.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In voce exsultatiónis * résonent epulántes in mensa Dómini.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let them that keep holiday around the table of the Lord * make the voice of joy and praise to be heard [in the house of God.]

Ant Matutinum.ant: Introíbo * ad altáre Dei: sumam Christum, qui rénovat juventútem meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I will go unto the Altar of God * I will feed on Christ, Which is the Renewer of my youth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cibávit nos Dóminus * ex ádipe fruménti: et de petra, melle saturávit nos.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath fed us * with the finest of the wheat, and with honey out of the Rock hath He satisfied us.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ex altári tuo, * Dómine, Christum súmimus: in quem cor et caro nostra exsúltant.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: It is at thine Altar, O Lord, * that we do feed on Christ, for Whom our heart and our flesh crieth out.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sacérdos in ætérnum * Christus Dóminus secúndum órdinem Melchísedech, panem et vinum óbtulit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Christ the Lord, being made an High Priest for ever * after the order of Melchisedec, hath offered bread and wine.

Ant Vespera.ant: Miserátor Dóminus * escam dedit timéntibus se in memóriam suórum mirabílium.
Ant Vespera.antEng: He hath made His wonderful works to be remembered; * the Lord is gracious and full of compassion. He hath given meat unto them that fear Him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cálicem salutáris * accípiam: et sacrificábo hóstiam laudis.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will take the cup of salvation, * and offer the sacrifice of thanksgiving.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sicut novéllæ olivárum, * Ecclésiæ fílii sint in circúitu mensæ Dómini.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Let the children of the Church be like olive-plants * round about the table of the Lord.

Ant Vespera.ant: Qui pacem * ponit fines Ecclésiæ, fruménti ádipe sátiat nos Dóminus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord, That maketh peace in the borders of the Church, * filleth her with the finest of the wheat.

Ant Laudes.ant: Unus mílitum * láncea latus ejus apéruit et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.
Ant Laudes.antEng: One of the soldiers * with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out Blood and Water.

Ant Laudes.ant: Stans Jesus * clamábat dicens: Si quis sitit, véniat ad me et bibat.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Jesus stood * and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.

Ant Laudes.ant: In caritáte perpétua * diléxit nos Deus, ídeo, exaltátus a terra, attráxit nos ad Cor suum, míserans.
Ant Laudes.antEng: With an everlasting love * hath God loved us, and from the day that he was lifted up over the earth, he hath drawn us with loving-kindness unto his Heart.

Ant Laudes.ant: Veníte ad me * omnes qui laborátis et oneráti estis et ego refíciam vos.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Come unto me, * all ye that travail and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fili, * præbe mihi cor tuum, et óculi tui custódiant vias meas.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My son, * give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cogitatiónes * Cordis ejus in generatióne et generatiónem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The thoughts of his Heart * shall endure from generation to generation.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Apud te * est fons vitæ; torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis nos, Dómine.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: For with thee * is the well of life, O Lord; and thou shalt give them drink of thy pleasures.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Homo * pacis meæ, qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Even mine own familiar friend * who did eat of my Bread, hath laid great wait for me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Rex omnis terræ * Deus; regnábit super gentes.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God is King * upon all the earth: he reigneth over the heathen.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dum anxiarétur * Cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When my Heart * was in heaviness, thou didst set me up upon a rock.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Secúndum multitúdinem * dolórum meórum in Corde meo, consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the multitude * of the sorrows that I had in my Heart, thy comforts have given joy to my soul.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Qui dilígitis Dóminum, * confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O ye that love the Lord, * give thanks for a remembrance of his holiness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vidérunt * omnes términi terræ salutáre Dei nostri.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All the ends of the world * have seen the salvation of our God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Psallam tibi * in natiónibus, quia magna est super cælos misericórdia tua.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I will sing praises unto thee * among the nations, for thy mercy is greater than the heavens.

Ant Vespera.ant: Suávi jugo tuo * domináre, Dómine, in médio inimicórum tuórum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Put thy easy yoke * upon all mankind, O Lord, and be thou ruler, even in the midst of thine enemies.

Ant Vespera.ant: Miséricors * et miserátor Dóminus: escam dedit timéntibus se.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This merciful * and gracious Lord hath given Meat unto them that fear him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis; miséricors et miserátor Dóminus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Unto the godly * there ariseth up light in the darkness, even the Lord merciful and gracious.

Ant Vespera.ant: Quid retríbuam * Dómino pro ómnibus quæ retríbuit mihi?
Ant Vespera.antEng: What reward shall I give * unto the Lord for all the benefits that he hath done unto me?

Ant Vespera.ant: Apud Dóminum * propitiátio est et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Unus mílitum * láncea latus ejus apéruit et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: One of the soldiers * with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out Blood and Water.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Stans Jesus * clamábat dicens: Si quis sitit, véniat ad me et bibat.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Jesus stood * and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: In caritáte perpétua * diléxit nos Deus, ídeo, exaltátus a terra, attráxit nos ad Cor suum, míserans.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: With an everlasting love * hath God loved us, and from the day that he was lifted up over the earth, he hath drawn us with loving-kindness unto his Heart.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Veníte ad me * omnes qui laborátis et oneráti estis et ego refíciam vos.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Come unto me, * all ye that travail and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Fili, * præbe mihi cor tuum, et óculi tui custódiant vias meas.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: My son, * give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

Ant Laudes.ant: Díscite a me, * quia mitis sum et húmilis corde.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Learn of Me, * for I am meek and lowly in Heart.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sanctificávi locum * istum, ut sit nomen meum ibi in sempitérnum, et permáneant óculi mei et cor meum ibi cunctis diébus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I have sanctified this place, * that My Name may be there for ever, and Mine eyes, and Mine heart shall be there perpetually.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et dixi: * Ergo sine causa justificávi cor meum, et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas, et fui flagellátus tota die.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And I said: Then have I cleansed my heart * in vain, and washed my hands in innocency, for all the day long have I been plagued.

Ant Laudes.ant: Secúndum multitúdinem * dolórum meórum in corde meo, consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In the multitude of the sorrows * within my heart, thy comforts delight my soul.

Ant Laudes.ant: Pone me * ut signáculum super cor tuum, ut signáculum super bráchium tuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, * as a seal upon thine arm.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Quid est homo * quia magníficas eum, aut quid appónis erga eum cor tuum?
Ant Matutinum.antEng: What is man, that Thou shouldest magnify him? and that Thou shouldest set thine Heart upon him?

Ant Matutinum.ant: Meditátio * cordis mei in conspéctu tuo sempe.r
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let the meditation of my heart be acceptable in thy sight for ever

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors, and the King of glory shall come in

Ant Matutinum.ant: Afferéntur * in lætítia et exsultatióne: adducéntur in templum Regis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought; they shall enter into the King's palace

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sanctificávit * tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Most High hath hallowed His Tabernacle

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sicut lætántium * ómnium habitátio est in te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All they that dwell in thee are in gladness

Ant Matutinum.ant: Annuntiáte * de die in diem salutáre ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Show forth His salvation from day to day

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adoráte eum * omnes Angeli ejus: audívit, et lætáta est Sion.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Worship Him, all ye His Angels Zion heard, and was glad

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vidérunt omnes * términi terræ salutáre Dei nostri.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God

Ant Vespera.ant: Díscite a me, * quia mitis sum et húmilis corde
Ant Vespera.antEng: Learn of Me, * for I am meek and lowly in Heart

Ant Vespera.ant: Sanctificávi locum * istum, ut sit nomen meum ibi in sempitérnum, et permáneant óculi mei et cor meum ibi cunctis diébus.

Ant Vespera.antEng: And I said: Then have I cleansed my heart * in vain, and washed my hands in innocence, for all the day long have I been plagued

Ant Vespera.ant: Secúndum multitúdinem * dolórum meórum in corde meo, consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam
Ant Vespera.antEng: In the multitude of the sorrows * within my heart, thy comforts delight my soul

Ant Vespera.ant: Pone me * ut signáculum super cor tuum, ut signáculum super bráchium tuum
Ant Vespera.antEng: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, * as a seal upon thine arm

Ant Laudes.ant: Cor mundum * crea in me Deus, et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Create in me a clean heart, * O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

Ant Laudes.ant: O Dómine, * salvum me fac; o Dómine, bene prosperáre.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Save me now, O Lord; * O Lord, send Thou prosperity.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sic benedícam * te in vita mea, Dómine: et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thus will I bless thee, * O Lord, while I live; and will lift up my hands in thy Name.

Ant Laudes.ant: In spíritu humilitátis, * et in ánimo contríto suscipiámur, Dómine, a te: et sic fiat sacrifícium nostrum, ut a te suscipiátur hódie, et pláceat tibi, Dómine Deus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In an humble spirit * and a contrite heart may we be accepted by thee, O Lord; and so let our sacrifice be this day, that it may be acceptable and pleasant in thy sight, O Lord our God!

Ant Laudes.ant: Laudáte Deum * cæli cælórum, et aquæ omnes.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise God, * ye heavens of heavens, and all ye waters.

Ant Nona.ant: Dóminum Deum tuum * adorábis, et illi soli sérvies.
Ant Nona.antEng: Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, * and Him only shalt thou serve.

Ant Prima.ant: Jesus autem * cum jejunásset quadragínta diébus et quadragínta nóctibus, póstea esúriit.
Ant Prima.antEng: When Jesus had fasted forty days * and forty nights, He was afterward hungry.

Ant Sexta.ant: Non in solo pane * vivit homo, sed in omni verbo, quod procédit de ore Dei.
Ant Sexta.antEng: Man shall not live by bread alone, * but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

Ant Tertia.ant: Tunc assúmpsit * eum diábolus in sanctam civitátem, et státuit eum supra pinnáculum templi, et dixit ei: Si Fílius Dei es, mitte te deórsum.
Ant Tertia.antEng: Then the devil taketh Him up into the holy city, * and setteth Him on a pinnacle of the temple, and saith unto Him: If Thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dómine, * lábia mea apéries, et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, open Thou my lips, * and my mouth shall show forth thy praise.

Ant Laudes.ant: Déxtera Dómini * fecit virtútem: déxtera Dómini exaltávit me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The right hand of the Lord * hath done valiantly, the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Factus est * adjútor meus, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My God * hath been my help.

Ant Laudes.ant: Trium puerórum * cantémus hymnum, quem cantábant in camíno ignis, benedicéntes Dóminum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let us sing the Song of the Three Children, * even the Song that they sang when they blessed the Lord in the burning fiery furnace.

Ant Laudes.ant: Státuit ea * in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: He hath established them * for ever and ever: He hath made a decree which shall not pass.

Ant Nona.ant: Visiónem quam vidístis, * némini dixéritis, donec a mórtuis resúrgat Fílius hóminis.
Ant Nona.antEng: Tell the vision that ye have seen to no man, * until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.

Ant Prima.ant: Dómine, * bonum est nos hic esse: si vis, faciámus hic tria tabernácula; tibi unum, Móysi unum, et Elíæ unum.
Ant Prima.antEng: Lord, it is good for us to be here; * if Thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Ant Sexta.ant: Faciámus hic * tria tabernácula; tibi unum, Móysi unum, et Elíæ unum.
Ant Sexta.antEng: Let us make here three tabernacles, * one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Ant Tertia.ant: Dómine, * bonum est nos hic esse: si vis, faciámus hic tria tabernácula; tibi unum, Móysi unum, et Elíæ unum.
Ant Tertia.antEng: Lord, it is good for us to be here; * if Thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Ant Laudes.antEng: The right hand of the Lord * hath done valiantly, the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Factus est * adjútor meus, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My God * hath been my help.

Ant Prima.antEng: Lord, it is good for us to be here; * if Thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Ant Sexta.ant: Faciámus hic * tria tabernácula; tibi unum, Móysi unum, et Elíæ unum.
Ant Sexta.antEng: Let us make here three tabernacles, * one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Ant Tertia.ant: Dómine, * bonum est nos hic esse: si vis, faciámus hic tria tabernácula; tibi unum, Móysi unum, et Elíæ unum.
Ant Tertia.antEng: Lord, it is good for us to be here; * if Thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fac benígne * in bona voluntáte tua, ut ædificéntur, Dómine, muri Jerúsalem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, do good in thy good pleasure * unto Zion; to build the walls of Jerusalem.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus * mihi adjútor est, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord is on my side; * I will not fear what can man do unto me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Adhǽsit ánima mea * post te, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O my God, my soul cleaveth fast * after thee, O God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vim virtútis suæ * oblítus est ignis: ut púeri tui liberaréntur illǽsi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The fire forgot his strength * that thy children might be delivered therefrom.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sol et luna * laudáte Deum: quia exaltátum est nomen ejus solíus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise God, O ye sun and moon, * for His Name alone is exalted!

Ant Nona.ant: Cum immúndus spíritus * exíerit ab hómine, ámbulat per loca inaquósa, quærens réquiem et non ínvenit.
Ant Nona.antEng: When the unclean spirit * is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and finding none.

Ant Prima.ant: Et cum ejecísset Jesus * dæmónium, locútus est mutus, et admirátæ sunt turbæ.
Ant Prima.antEng: When Jesus had cast out the devil, * the dumb spake, and the people wondered.

Ant Sexta.ant: Qui non cólligit mecum * dispérgit, et qui non est mecum, contra me est.
Ant Sexta.antEng: He that gathereth not with Me scattereth, * and he that is not with Me is against Me.

Ant Tertia.ant: Si in dígito Dei * eício dæmónia, profécto pervénit in vos regnum Dei.
Ant Tertia.antEng: If I with the finger of God * cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tunc acceptábis * sacrifícium justítiæ, si avérteris fáciem tuam a peccátis meis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Then shalt Thou be pleased * with the sacrifices of righteousness, when Thou hast hidden thy face from my sins.

Ant Laudes.ant: Bonum est * speráre in Dómino, quam speráre in princípibus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: It is better to trust * in the Lord, than to trust in princes.

Ant Laudes.ant: Me suscépit * déxtera tua, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thy right hand hath * received me, O Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Potens es, Dómine, * erípere nos de manu forti: líbera nos, Deus noster.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou art mighty * to save us; with a strong hand deliver us, O our God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Reges terræ * et omnes pópuli, laudáte Deum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Kings of the earth, * and all people, praise God.

Ant Nona.ant: Illi ergo * hómines, cum vidíssent quod fécerat Jesus signum, intra se dicébant: quia hic est vere Prophéta, qui ventúrus est in mundum.
Ant Nona.antEng: Then those men, * when they had seen the miracle that Jesus did, said amongst themselves: This is of a truth that Prophet that should come into the world.

Ant Prima.ant: Accépit ergo * Jesus panes, et, cum grátias egísset, distríbuit discumbéntibus.
Ant Prima.antEng: And Jesus took the loaves, * and when He had given thanks, He distributed to them that were set down.

Ant Sexta.ant: Satiávit Dóminus * quinque míllia hóminum de quinque pánibus et duobus píscibus.
Ant Sexta.antEng: With five loaves and two fishes * did the Lord satisfy five thousand men.

Ant Tertia.ant: De quinque pánibus * et duobus píscibus satiávit Dóminus quinque míllia hóminum.
Ant Tertia.antEng: With five loaves and two fishes * did the Lord satisfy five thousand men.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tunc acceptábis * sacrifícium justítiæ, si avérteris fáciem tuam a peccátis meis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Then shalt Thou be pleased * with the sacrifices of righteousness, when Thou hast hidden thy face from my sins.

Ant Laudes.antEng: Thy right hand hath * received me, O Lord.

Ant Sexta.antEng: With five loaves and two fishes * did the Lord satisfy five thousand men.

Ant Tertia.ant: De quinque pánibus * et duobus píscibus satiávit Dóminus quinque míllia hóminum.
Ant Tertia.antEng: With five loaves and two fishes * did the Lord satisfy five thousand men.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vide, Dómine, * afflictiónem meam, quóniam eréctus est inimícus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, behold my affliction; * for the enemy hath magnified himself.

Ant Laudes.ant: In tribulatióne * invocávi Dóminum, et exaudívit me in latitúdine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I called upon the Lord * in my distress; and He answered me, and set me at large.

Ant Laudes.ant: Judicásti, Dómine, * causam ánimæ meæ, defénsor vitæ meæ, Dómine Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast pleaded the cause of my soul; * Thou hast redeemed my life, O Lord my God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Pópule meus, * quid feci tibi, aut quid moléstus fui? Respónde mihi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O My people, what have I done unto thee? * or wherein have I wearied thee? testify against Me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Numquid rédditur * pro bono malum, quia fodérunt fóveam ánimæ meæ.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Shall evil be recompensed for good? * for they have digged a pit for My soul.

Ant Nona.ant: Tulérunt lápides * Judǽi, ut jácerent in eum: Jesus autem abscóndit se, et exívit de templo.
Ant Nona.antEng: Then took the Jews up stones * to cast at Him, but Jesus hid Himself, and went out of the temple.

Ant Prima.ant: Ego dæmónium non hábeo, * sed honorífico Patrem meum, dicit Dóminus.
Ant Prima.antEng: I have not a devil; * but I honour My Father, and ye do dishonour Me, saith the Lord.

Ant Sexta.ant: Amen, amen, dico vobis: * si quis sermónem meum serváverit, mortem non gustábit in ætérnum.
Ant Sexta.antEng: Amen, Amen, * I say unto you: If a man keep My saying, he shall never see death.

Ant Tertia.ant: Ego glóriam meam * non quæro: est qui quærat, et júdicet.
Ant Tertia.antEng: I seek not Mine Own glory; * there is One That seeketh and judgeth.

Ant Tertia.antEng: I seek not Mine Own glory; * there is One That seeketh and judgeth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vadam ad montem * myrrhæ et ad collem thuris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, * and to the hill of frankincense.

Ant Laudes.ant: Diléctus meus * cándidus et rubicúndus: comæ cápitis ejus sicut púrpura regis vincta canálibus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My beloved * is white and ruddy the hair of his head is like kingly purple, bound in tresses.

Ant Laudes.ant: Quo ábiit * diléctus tuus, o pulchérrima mulíerum? quo diléctus tuus declinávit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Whither is thy beloved gone, * O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside?

Ant Laudes.ant: Fascículus myrrhæ * diléctus meus mihi inter úbera mea commorábitur.
Ant Laudes.antEng: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie betwixt my breasts.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fulcíte me flóribus * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples, for I am swooning with love.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Astitérunt reges terræ, * et príncipes convenérunt in unum advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together against the Lord, and against His Anointed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Voce mea * ad Dóminum clamávi, et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I cried unto the Lord with my voice, and He heard me out of His holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factum est cor meum * tamquam cera liquéscens in médio ventris mei.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My heart is like melting wax in the midst of my bowels.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Inimíci mei * dixérunt mala mihi: Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Mine enemies speak evil of me When shall he die, and his name perish.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus, vitam meam * annuntiávi tibi: posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O God, I have declared my life unto thee, Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Fílii hóminum, * dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: As for the sons of men, their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Intendérunt arcum, * rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They bend their bow, even bitter words, that they may shoot in secret at the perfect.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factus sum * sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am as a man that hath no strength, lying nerveless among the dead.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Replévit me amaritúdine, * inebriávit me absýnthio.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vadam ad montem * myrrhæ et ad collem thuris.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, * and to the hill of frankincense.

Ant Vespera.ant: Diléctus meus * cándidus et rubicúndus: comæ cápitis ejus sicut púrpura regis vincta canálibus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: My beloved * is white and ruddy; the hair of his head is like kingly purple, bound in tresses.

Ant Vespera.ant: Quo ábiit * diléctus tuus, o pulchérrima mulíerum? quo diléctus tuus declinávit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Whither is thy beloved gone, * O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside?

Ant Vespera.ant: Fascículus myrrhæ * diléctus meus mihi inter úbera mea commorábitur.
Ant Vespera.antEng: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie betwixt my breasts.

Ant Vespera.ant: Fulcíte me flóribus * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples, for I am swooning with love.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus Deus * auxiliátor meus: et ídeo non sum confúsus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord God will help me * and therefore I am not confounded.

Ant Laudes.ant: Circumdántes * circumdedérunt me: et in nómine Dómini vindicábor in eis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: They compassed me about, * yea, they compassed me about but in the Name of the Lord! I will destroy them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Júdica causam meam: * defénde, quia potens es, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Judge Thou my cause, * and redeem me, O Lord, for Thou art mighty to save.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cum Angelis * et púeris fidéles inveniámur, triumphatóri mortis clamántes: Hosánna in excélsis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Fare we with Angels and men in faith to meet the Redeemer, * hailing the Slayer of death with joyful shouts of “Hosanna in the highest!”

Ant Laudes.ant: Confundántur * qui me persequúntur, et non confúndar ego, Dómine, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let them be confounded that persecute me; * but let not me be confounded, O Lord my God.

Ant Nona.ant: Invocábo * nomen tuum, Dómine: ne avértas fáciem tuam a clamóre meo.
Ant Nona.antEng: I will call * upon thy Name, O Lord: hide not thy face at my cry.

Ant Prima.ant: Púeri Hebræórum * tolléntes ramos olivárum, obviavérunt Dómino clamántes et dicéntes: Hosánna in excélsis.
Ant Prima.antEng: The Hebrew children took branches of olive-trees, * and went forth to meet the Lord, crying and saying: Hosanna in the highest!

Ant Sexta.ant: Tibi revelávi * causam meam, defénsor vitæ meæ, Dómine, Deus meus.
Ant Sexta.antEng: Unto thee have I opened my cause, * O Lord my God, Which art the Redeemer of my life.

Ant Tertia.ant: Púeri Hebræórum * vestiménta prosternébant in via, et clamábant, dicéntes: Hosánna Fílio David: benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini.
Ant Tertia.antEng: The Hebrew children spread their garments in the way, * and cried, saying: Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He that cometh in the Name of the Lord!

Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord God will help me * and therefore I am not confounded.

Ant Prima.antEng: The Hebrew children took branches of olive-trees, * and went forth to meet the Lord, crying and saying: Hosanna in the highest!

Ant Sexta.antEng: Unto thee have I opened my cause, * O Lord my God, Which art the Redeemer of my life.
