Ant Tertia.antEng: The Hebrew children spread their garments in the way, * and cried, saying: Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He that cometh in the Name of the Lord!

Ant Laudes.ant: Fáciem meam * non avérti ab increpántibus, et conspuéntibus in me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I hid not my face * from shame and spitting.

Ant Laudes.ant: Frámea, suscitáre * advérsus eos, qui dispérgunt gregem meum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Awake, O sword, * against them that scatter my flock.

Ant Laudes.ant: Appendérunt * mercédem meam trigínta argénteis: quibus appretiátus sum ab eis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: They took the thirty pieces of silver, * my price, that I was prized at of them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Inundavérunt aquæ * super caput meum: dixi, Périi: invocábo nomen tuum, Dómine Deus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Waters flowed over mine head; * I said I am cut off; I will call upon thy Name, O Lord God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lábia insurgéntium, * et cogitatiónes eórum vide, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, behold the lips * of those that rose up against me, and their device.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vide, Dómine, * et consídera, quóniam tríbulor: velóciter exáudi me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, O Lord, and see, * for I am in trouble; hear me speedily.

Ant Laudes.ant: Discérne causam meam, * Dómine: ab hómine iníquo et dolóso éripe me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Plead my cause, * O Lord; deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dum tribulárer, * clamávi ad Dóminum de ventre ínferi, et exaudívit me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, * and He heard me out of the belly of hell.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dómine, vim pátior, * respónde pro me: quia néscio quid dicam inimícis meis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, I am oppressed, * undertake Thou for me; for I know not what to say unto mine enemies.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dixérunt ímpii: * Opprimámus virum justum, quóniam contrárius est opéribus nostris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The ungodly said Let us oppress the righteous man, * because he is clean contrary to our doings.

Ant Laudes.ant: Líbera me * de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus meus: et exsultábit lingua mea justítiam tuam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Deliver me * from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall extol thy justice.

Ant Laudes.ant: Contumélias * et terróres passus sum ab eis: et Dóminus mecum est tamquam bellátor fortis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I received * injuries and terrors from them: but the Lord is with me as a strong warrior.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tu autem, Dómine, * scis omne consílium eórum advérsum me in mortem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: But thou, O Lord, * knowest all their plans to put me to death.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnes inimíci mei * audiérunt malum meum: Dómine, lætáti sunt, quóniam tu fecísti.
Ant Laudes.antEng: All my enemies have heard of my evil, * they have rejoiced that thou, O Lord, hast done it.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fac, Dómine, * judícium injúriam patiéntibus: et vias peccatórum dispérde.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord helpeth them * to right that suffer wrong, but as for the way of the ungodly, he turneth it upside down.

Ant Laudes.ant: Justificéris, Dómine, * in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum judicáris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou shalt be justified * when Thou speakest, and be clear when Thou art judged.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus * tamquam ovis ad víctimam ductus est, et non apéruit os suum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord was brought as a lamb * to the slaughter, and He opened not His mouth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Contrítum est * cor meum in médio mei, contremuérunt ómnia ossa mea.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Mine heart is broken within me * all my bones tremble.

Ant Laudes.ant: Exhortátus es * in virtúte tua, et in refectióne sancta tua, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast spoken unto us * in thy strength, and in thy Holy Banquet.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oblátus est * quia ipse vóluit, et peccáta nostra ipse portávit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: He was offered up because He willed it * and He bore our sins.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Zelus domus tuæ * comédit me, et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The zeal of thine house * hath eaten me up, and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Avertántur retrórsum, * et erubéscant, qui cógitant mihi mala.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let them be turned backward * and put to confusion that desire my hurt.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus meus, * éripe me de manu peccatóris.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Deliver me, my God, * out of the hand of the wicked.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Liberávit Dóminus * páuperem a poténte, et ínopem, cui non erat adjútor.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord shall deliver * the needy from the strong: the poor also, that hath no helper.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cogitavérunt ímpii, * et locúti sunt nequítiam: iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The ungodly think * and speak wickedness: they speak loftily concerning oppression.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Exsúrge, Dómine, * et júdica causam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Arise, O Lord, * and judge my cause.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dixi iníquis: * Nolíte loqui advérsus Deum iniquitátem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I said unto the wicked: * Speak not wickedness against God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Terra trémuit * et quiévit, dum exsúrgeret in judício Deus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The earth trembled * and was still, when God arose to judgment.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In die tribulatiónis * meæ Deum exquisívi mánibus meis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the day of my trouble * I sought God with my hands.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cálicem * salutáris accípiam et nomen Dómini invocábo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will take the cup of salvation; * and call upon the Name of the Lord.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cum his, * qui odérunt pacem eram pacíficus: dum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With them * that hate peace I was peaceable; when I spoke unto them they fought against me without a cause.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ab homínibus * iníquis líbera me, Dómine.
Ant Vespera.antEng: O Lord, preserve me * from the wicked man.

Ant Vespera.ant: Custódi me * a láqueo, quem statuérunt mihi, et a scándalis operántium iniquitátem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Keep me * from the snare which they have laid for me, and the gins of the workers of iniquity.

Ant Vespera.ant: Considerábam * ad déxteram, et vidébam, et non erat qui cognósceret me.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I looked * on my right hand and beheld: but there was no man that would know me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Justificéris, Dómine, * in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum judicáris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou shalt be justified * when Thou speakest, and be clear when Thou art judged.

Ant Laudes.ant: Próprio * Fílio suo non pepércit Deus, sed pro nobis ómnibus trádidit illum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: God spared not His Own Son * but delivered Him up for us all.

Ant Laudes.ant: Anxiátus est super me * spíritus meus, in me turbátum est cor meum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My spirit is overwhelmed within me; * my heart within me is troubled.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ait latro ad latrónem: * Nos quidem digna factis recípimus, hic autem quid fecit? Meménto mei, Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: One thief said unto the other: * We indeed receive the due reward of our deeds, but what hath this man done? Lord, remember me, when thou comest into thy kingdom.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cum conturbáta fúerit * ánima mea, Dómine, misericórdiæ memor eris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lord, when my soul is troubled, * thou wilt remember mercy.

Ant Laudes.ant: Meménto mei, * Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lord, remember me * when thou comest into thy kingdom.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Astitérunt reges terræ, * et príncipes convenérunt in unum, advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The kings of the earth set themselves, * and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against His Anointed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Divisérunt sibi * vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They part my garments among them, * and cast lots upon my vesture.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Insurrexérunt in me * testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: False witnesses are risen up against me, * and iniquity hath belied itself.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vim faciébant, * qui quærébant ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They that sought after my life * have used violence again me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Confundántur * et revereántur, qui quærunt ánimam meam, ut áuferant eam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let them be ashamed and confounded * together that seek after my soul, to destroy it.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Aliéni * insurrexérunt in me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Strangers are risen up against me, * and oppressors seek after my soul.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ab insurgéntibus in me * líbera me, Dómine, quia occupavérunt ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, defend me from them that rise up against me, * for they lie in wait for my life.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Longe fecísti * notos meos a me: tráditus sum, et non egrediébar.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me; * I am shut up, and cannot come forth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Captábunt * in ánimam justi, et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They gather themselves together * against the soul of the righteous, and condemn the innocent blood.

Ant Laudes.ant: O mors, * ero mors tua, morsus tuus ero, inférne.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O death, I will be thy death; * O grave, I will be thy destruction.

Ant Laudes.ant: Plangent eum * quasi unigénitum, quia ínnocens Dóminus occísus est.
Ant Laudes.antEng: They shall mourn for Him * as one mourneth for his only son, for the innocent Lord hath been put to death.

Ant Laudes.ant: Atténdite * univérsi pópuli, et vidéte dolórem meum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O all ye nations, behold * and see my sorrow.

Ant Laudes.ant: A porta ínferi * érue, Dómine, ánimam meam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, deliver my soul * from the gates of the grave.

Ant Laudes.ant: O vos omnes, * qui transítis per viam, atténdite et vidéte, si est dolor sicut dolor meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O all ye that pass by * behold, and see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In pace * in idípsum, dórmiam et requiéscam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I will both lay me down in peace, * and sleep.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Habitábit * in tabernáculo tuo, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He shall abide in thy tabernacle: * he shall dwell in thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Caro mea * requiéscet in spe.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My flesh * shall rest in hope.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be ye lift up, * ye everlasting doors, and the King of glory shall come in.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Credo vidére * bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I believe that I shall yet see * the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, * abstraxísti ab ínferis ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast brought up * my soul from the grave.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus ádjuvat me, * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God is my helper, * and the Lord upholdeth my soul.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In pace * factus est locus ejus, et in Sion habitátio ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: His place is in peace * and His dwelling-place in Zion.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factus sum * sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am as a man that hath no strength, * lying nerveless among the dead.

Ant Laudes.ant: O mors, * ero mors tua, morsus tuus ero, inférne.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O death, I will be thy death; * O grave, I will be thy destruction.

Ant Laudes.ant: Plangent eum * quasi unigénitum, quia ínnocens Dóminus occísus est.
Ant Laudes.antEng: They shall mourn for Him * as one mourneth for his only son, for the innocent Lord hath been put to death.

Ant Laudes.ant: Atténdite * univérsi pópuli, et vidéte dolórem meum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O all ye nations, behold * and see my sorrow.

Ant Laudes.ant: A porta ínferi * érue, Dómine, ánimam meam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, deliver my soul * from the gates of the grave.

Ant Laudes.ant: O vos omnes, * qui transítis per viam, atténdite et vidéte, si est dolor sicut dolor meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O all ye that pass by * behold, and see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In pace * in idípsum, dórmiam et requiéscam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I will both lay me down in peace, * and sleep.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Habitábit * in tabernáculo tuo, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He shall abide in thy tabernacle: * he shall dwell in thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Caro mea * requiéscet in spe.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My flesh * shall rest in hope.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be ye lift up, * ye everlasting doors, and the King of glory shall come in.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Credo vidére * bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I believe that I shall yet see * the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, * abstraxísti ab ínferis ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast brought up * my soul from the grave.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus ádjuvat me, * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God is my helper, * and the Lord upholdeth my soul.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In pace * factus est locus ejus, et in Sion habitátio ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: His place is in peace * and His dwelling-place in Zion.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factus sum * sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am as a man that hath no strength, * lying nerveless among the dead.

Ant Vespera.ant: Hódie afflíctus sum valde, * sed cras solvam víncula mea.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Today I am greatly afflicted, * but tomorrow I will break my bonds.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cum his, * qui odérunt pacem, eram pacíficus: dum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With them * that hated peace I was peaceable: when I spoke to them they fought against me without cause.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ab homínibus * iníquis líbera me, Dómine.
Ant Vespera.antEng: From unjust men * deliver me, O Lord.

Ant Vespera.ant: Custódi me * a láqueo, quem statuérunt mihi, et a scándalis operántium iniquitátem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Keep me * from the snare, which they have laid for me, and from the stumbling-blocks of them that work iniquity.

Ant Vespera.ant: Considerábam * ad déxteram, et vidébam, et non erat qui cognósceret me.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I looked * on my right hand, and beheld, and there was no one that would know me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Miserére * mei, Deus, et a delícto meo munda me: quia tibi soli peccávi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Have mercy upon me, * O God, and cleanse me from my sin, for against thee only have I sinned.

Ant Laudes.ant: Confitébor * tibi, quóniam exaudísti me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I will praise thee, * for thou hast heard me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo, quia factus es adjútor meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O God, Thou art my God, * early will I seek thee, because thou hast been my help.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíctus es * in firmaménto cæli, et laudábilis in sǽcula, Deus noster.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed art thou, * O our God, in the firmament of heaven, and worthy to be praised above all for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Laudáte * Dóminum de cælis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise ye the Lord * from the heavens.

Ant Nona.ant: Voca operários, * et redde illis mercédem suam, dicit Dóminus.
Ant Nona.antEng: The Lord of the vineyard saith * Call the labourers, and give them their hire.

Ant Prima.ant: Conventióne autem * facta cum operáriis ex denário diúrno, misit eos in víneam suam.
Ant Prima.antEng: And when he had agreed * with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

Ant Sexta.ant: Quid hic statis * tota die otiósi? respondérunt, et dixérunt: Quia nemo nos condúxit.
Ant Sexta.antEng: Why stand ye here * all the day idle? They answered and said unto him: Because no man hath hired us.

Ant Tertia.ant: Ite et vos * in víneam meam, et quod justum fúerit, dabo vobis.
Ant Tertia.antEng: Go ye also * into my vineyard, and whatsoever is right, that will I give you.

Ant Laudes.ant: Secúndum magnam misericórdiam * tuam miserére mei, Deus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Have mercy upon me, O God, * after thy great mercy.

Ant Laudes.ant: Si mihi Dóminus * salvátor fúerit, non timébo, quid fáciat mihi homo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: If the Lord be my Saviour * I will not fear what man can do unto me.

Ant Laudes.ant: In velaménto * clamávi valde dilúculo: Deus, Deus meus, ad te de luce vígilo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Within the veil I cried betimes: * O God, Thou art my God, early will I seek thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hymnum dicámus * Dómino Deo nostro.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let us sing praises * to the Lord our God.

Ant Laudes.ant: In excélsis, * laudáte Deum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In the high places, * praise ye God.

Ant Nona.ant: Si vere, fratres, * dívites esse cúpitis, veras divítias amáte.
Ant Nona.antEng: If then, dearly beloved brethren, ye seek to be rich, * earnestly desire the true riches.

Ant Prima.ant: Semen cécidit * in terram bonam, et áttulit fructum in patiéntia.
Ant Prima.antEng: The seed fell * upon good ground, and brought forth its fruit in patience.

Ant Sexta.ant: Semen cécidit * in terram bonam, et áttulit fructum, áliud centésimum, et áliud sexagésimum.
Ant Sexta.antEng: Some seed fell on good ground, * and bare fruit, some one hundred-fold, and some sixty-fold.

Ant Tertia.ant: Qui verbum Dei * rétinent corde perfécto et óptimo, fructum áfferunt in patiéntia.
Ant Tertia.antEng: They who keep * the word of God with a good and perfect heart, bring forth fruit in patience.

Ant Laudes.ant: Secúndum multitúdinem * miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, dele iniquitátem meam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, according to the multitude of thy tender mercies, * blot out my transgressions.

Ant Laudes.ant: Deus meus es tu, * et confitébor tibi: Deus meus es tu, et exaltábo te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou art my God, * and I will praise thee; Thou art my God, and I will exalt thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ad te de luce * vígilo, Deus, ut vídeam virtútem tuam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O God, early will I seek thee, * to see thy power.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hymnum dícite, * et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Sing praises, * and exalt Him above all for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnes Angeli * ejus laudáte Dóminum de cælis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise ye the Lord * from the heavens, all His angels.

Ant Nona.ant: Cæcus magis * ac magis clamábat, ut eum Dóminus illumináret.
Ant Nona.antEng: The blind man cried to the Lord * so much the more, to give him light.

Ant Prima.ant: Iter faciénte * Jesu, dum appropinquáret Jericho, cæcus clamábat ad eum, ut lumen recípere mererétur.
Ant Prima.antEng: As Jesus went on His way, * as He was come nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man cried unto Him, that he might worthily receive his sight.

Ant Sexta.ant: Et qui præíbant, * increpábant eum ut tacéret: ipse vero multo magis clamábat: Miserére mei, Fili David.
Ant Sexta.antEng: And they that went before rebuked him, * that he should hold his peace, but he cried so much the more: Thou Son of David, have mercy on me!

Ant Tertia.ant: Transeúnte * Dómino, clamábat cæcus ad eum: Miserére mei, Fili David.
Ant Tertia.antEng: As the Lord passed by, * a certain blind man cried unto Him: Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Suscitábit * Deus cæli regnum quod commínuet et consúmet univérsa regna, et ipsum stabit in ætérnum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The God of heaven * will set up a kingdom that shall break in pieces and shall consume all these kingdoms, and itself shall stand for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dedit ei Dóminus * potestátem et honórem et regnum; et omnes pópuli, tribus et linguæ ipsi sérvient.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord gave him * power and glory, and a kingdom; and all peoples, tribes and tongues shall serve him.

Ant Laudes.ant: Exíbunt aquæ vivæ * de Jerúsalem; et erit Dóminus Rex super omnem terram.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Living waters shall go out * from Jerusalem; and the Lord shall be king over all the earth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Magnificábitur * usque ad términos terræ, et erit iste pax.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Now shall he be magnified * even to the ends of the earth, and this man shall be our peace.

Ant Laudes.ant: Gens et regnum * quod non servíerit tibi, períbit: et gentes solitúdine vastabúntur.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The nation and the kingdom * that will not serve thee, shall perish: and the Gentiles shall be wasted with desolation.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego autem * constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, prǽdicans præcéptum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I have been set up * as King by Him on Sion, His holy mountain, proclaiming His decree.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Glória * et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine: ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honor, O Lord, putting all things under His feet.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Reach up * you ancient portals, that the King of glory may come in.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sedébit * Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord is enthroned * as King forever; may the Lord bless his people with peace.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Virga directiónis, * virga regni tui: proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: A tempered rod * is thy royal scepter; therefore shall nations praise thee forever and ever.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Psállite * Regi nostro, psállite: quóniam Rex magnus super omnem terram.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing praise to our King * sing praise; for he is the great King over all earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Benedicéntur in ipso * omnes tribus terræ; omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In Him * shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed; all the nations shall proclaim His greatness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Et ego primogénitum * ponam illum: excélsum præ régibus terræ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And I will make Him * the firstborn, highest of the kings of the earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Thronus ejus * sicut sol in conspéctu meo: et sicut luna perfécta in ætérnum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: His throne * shall be like the sun before Me; like the moon, which remains forever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Pacíficus * vocábitur, et thronus ejus erit firmíssimus in perpétuum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: He shall be called * Peaceable, and his throne shall be most firm for ever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Regnum ejus * regnum sempitérnum est, et omnes reges sérvient ei et obédient.
Ant Vespera.antEng: His kingdom * is an everlasting kingdom, and all kings shall serve him, and shall obey him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce Vir Oriens * nomen ejus: sedébit et dominábitur, et loquétur pacem géntibus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold a man, the Orient * is his name: he shall sit and rule, and shall speak peace to the Gentiles.

Ant Vespera.ant: Dóminus * judex noster, Dóminus légifer noster: Dóminus Rex noster, ipse salvábit nos.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord * is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver: the Lord is our king, he will save us.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce dedi te * in lucem géntium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extrémum terræ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold, I have given thee * to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth.
